sections.heading: E-Sign
sections.text: @absolutejs/esign v0.0.1 beta Commerce & Growth Provider-neutral e-signature requests, sessions, status reconciliation, and webhook contracts

sections.heading: Installation
sections.text: BASH bun add @absolutejs/esign

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Provider-neutral electronic signing for Node.js and Bun. Own agreement versions, identities, permissions, persistence, and billing in your application; swap providers through the same signing contract. The initial adapters are @absolutejs/esign-docusign and @absolutejs/esign-dropbox-sign. Install only the adapters you use. This package has no provider SDK, database, UI framework, or implicit network initialization.

sections.heading: Contract
sections.text: createRequest: PDFs, signer identities, signature field placement, and an application reference. getRequest: current provider state and individual signer status. createSigningSession: short-lived access for a server-authorized signer already on that request. Show 5 more downloadCompleted: completed PDF; separate audit certificate when supported. cancelRequest: cancel the provider request. verifyWebhook: verify the provider's authentication and return a reconciliation hint. capabilities: embedded signing, ordered signing, cancellation, and separate audit downloads. Signature fields use one-based pages and provider document coordinates (72 DPI). Document/signer IDs are local identifiers; persist the provider signer IDs returned by createRequest. Always authorize by your saved participant-to-provider-signer mapping, never a caller-supplied email or signer ID.

sections.heading: Account connections
sections.text: linkedESignProvider(resolver, { ownerRef, provider, bindingId }, factory) accepts the existing @absolutejs/linked-providers resolver. It resolves the binding for that owner and supplies a fresh token callback to the adapter. The host stores and encrypts grants, refreshes tokens, and handles revocation. Provider OAuth helpers are also exported by each adapter; their caller must generate unpredictable state, bind it to the signed-in account, validate and consume it once, and persist tokens securely.

sections.heading: Durable workflow
sections.text: Save an immutable document revision and SHA-256 digest (documentDigest) before sending. Persist a creation operation before calling the provider. Do not automatically retry an ambiguous POST timeout; reconcile the operation before allowing another send. Save provider request and signer IDs against that revision. Do not change providers after a request is sent; cancel and create a new revision instead. Show 5 more Check ownership and recipient role before issuing a signing session. Verify callback authentication, deduplicate callback IDs, and call reconcileSignatureRequest using the saved request ID and reference. Callback bodies and browser return URLs never establish completion. Retrieve and persist the completed PDF and audit artifact when available. A completed request can precede PDF generation; retry artifact retrieval separately without re-sending. Dropbox Sign's event hash authenticates event time and type, not every payload field. Re-fetching the saved request is mandatory. Preserve terminal state against out-of-order callbacks; an interrupted refresh must not erase a known completed state. HTTP errors exclude vendor response bodies and access tokens. Creation POSTs are never automatically retried. All HTTP requests have bounded timeouts. Callback routes should enforce body-size limits and return each adapter's webhookAcknowledgement after durable processing.

sections.heading: Development
sections.text: bun run build, bun run typecheck; adapter contract tests live in ../esign-adapters/test. Tests inject fetch and make no external requests. Live account and sandbox acceptance tests are required before enabling a provider for real agreements. Outcomes

sections.heading: @absolutejs/esign-docusign
sections.text: @absolutejs/esign-docusign v0.0.1 beta Commerce & Growth DocuSign adapter for @absolutejs/esign

sections.heading: Installation
sections.text: BASH bun add @absolutejs/esign-docusign

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The base URI must be the HTTPS base_uri for the selected account returned by OAuth /userinfo, not a user-entered API URL. Sandbox uses https://account-d.docusign.com; production OAuth uses https://account.docusign.com. docusignOAuth provides authorization URL construction, code exchange, refresh, and account discovery. The application must validate OAuth state and authorize the selected account. Use a DocuSign integration key with an approved redirect URI and configure Connect HMAC secrets. Pass the exact raw JSON callback body and headers to verifyWebhook; key rotation is supported by passing multiple secrets. Reconcile the saved envelope afterward. authenticationMethod: none records that the application provides recipient authorization; it does not add provider identity verification. Signature requests use embedded recipients. Open createSigningSession().url as a top-level navigation, then reconcile after returning. Both combined PDF and completion certificate downloads require a completed envelope. Show 1 more References: Create envelope, recipient view, Connect HMAC. Outcomes

sections.heading: @absolutejs/esign-dropbox-sign
sections.text: @absolutejs/esign-dropbox-sign v0.0.1 beta Commerce & Growth Dropbox Sign adapter for @absolutejs/esign

sections.heading: Installation
sections.text: BASH bun add @absolutejs/esign-dropbox-sign

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Supports OAuth bearer tokens or an explicitly configured API key. OAuth tokens are distinct from the API key used to verify callback event hashes. dropboxSignOAuth provides authorization URLs, code exchange, refresh, and account discovery. The host must validate OAuth state and persist grants securely. Configure the API app's callback URL and allowed embedded domain. App approval is required for production embedded/OAuth use. Keep testMode: true until the app is approved and live verification is complete. Test-mode requests are not production signatures. Use the official hellosign-embedded browser client to open the returned signing URL with clientId; honor its documented domain checks and configured return flow. Do not treat a browser sign or close event as completion. Reconcile the saved request with the backend. Show 2 more Dropbox sends callbacks as multipart form data. Pass the exact json field to verifyWebhook. Return Hello API Event Received after processing. The HMAC covers event time/type only; always fetch the saved request again before updating agreement state. Completed-document downloads contain the audit trail; a separate audit endpoint is not offered by this adapter. References: Embedded signing, callback verification, OAuth, field placement. Outcomes

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: OAuth2 authentication with @absolutejs/auth, demonstrated across all six AbsoluteJS frontends — React, Vue, Svelte, Angular, HTML, and HTMX — backed by one Elysia server, one JSON/OAuth API, and one shared CSS file.

sections.heading: What it shows
sections.text: Every framework implements the same flows against the shared backend: OAuth / accounts (every framework): Sign in / sign up with any of 60 OAuth2 providers (one-tap buttons for a Show 10 more featured few, plus a full provider dropdown). Protected page that renders the authenticated user record. Settings — account overview, link additional login providers to the same canonical user, search/sort linked identities, set a primary identity, remove identities, resolve account-merge requests, and delete the account. Connectors — link Google (Gmail/Contacts) and Meta (Facebook/Instagram) data connectors, then view and revoke the resulting OAuth grants and the external accounts discovered for them. Post-OAuth surfaces (rolling out per framework — React first): Credentials — email + password sign-up / sign-in via createAuthClient, with HIBP breach check at register + login and disposable-domain rejection. Passkeys — WebAuthn conditional-UI autofill + "upgrade to passkey" prompt

sections.heading: Run it
sections.text: A Postgres database (e.g. Neon) is required — the session store and user data live there. providersConfiguration reads every provider's credentials from the environment, so set the providers you intend to demo. Showcase env vars (optional but recommended)

sections.heading: Installation
sections.text: BASH # Private workspace project: ~/abs/examples/demo

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Runnable product-demo proof for @absolutejs/demo. By default this starts a tiny local product fixture, drives it with Playwright, records the browser, adds narrator cues, highlights product UI, writes a manifest, and composes a final MP4 with FFmpeg. The demo opens with two real sign-ins, then runs the product walkthrough — all in one recording, composed into a single .mp4 per run: Show 8 more Your own site — the form profile drives the fixture's real login form (opens the auth tab, types email + password, submits, confirms authenticated). A third party you don't control — the form profile logs into saucedemo.com by driving its real login screen. Credentials are passed to the profiles as env references ({ env: "NAME" }), so values stay out of the script. This does not redact the login UI: review recordings and reports before sharing, and use demo accounts. They are required — the demo refuses to run without them (no silent defaults). Own-site values can be anything (the fixture accepts them). For the third party, saucedemo.com's documented public test login is standard_user / secret_sauce. Swap in real credentials + DEMO_TARGET_URL to point at your own app and a real third-party site. Each run writes to a timestamped directory under .demo-artifacts/, e.g. .demo-artifacts/absolute-product-demo-2026-05-28T193925Z/, containing the recording, screenshots, voiceover audio, manifest, and the composed …​.mp4 — review that single MP4 to see the whole run (sign-ins included). Voiceover uses the upgraded ElevenLabs path; ELEVENLABS_API_KEY loads from the local .env by default (set DEMO_ENV_FILE to load a different file). For a minimal browser-to-MP4 walkthrough without third-party sign-ins, use demo/examples/quick-start.ts. Set DEMO_COMPOSE=false to skip FFmpeg composition, DEMO_HEADLESS=1 to run without a visible browser. Outcomes

sections.heading: absolutejs-island-example
sections.text: absolutejs-island-example v0.0.1 beta Dev Tools An example project demonstrating the AbsoluteJS islands architecture — mix React, Svelte, Vue, Angular, HTML, and HTMX components on the same page with shared state across frameworks.

sections.heading: Installation

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: An example project demonstrating the AbsoluteJS islands architecture — mix React, Svelte, Vue, Angular, HTML, and HTMX components on the same page with shared state across frameworks.

sections.heading: What Are Islands?
sections.text: Islands architecture renders most of the page as static HTML on the server and selectively hydrates interactive "islands" on the client. Each island is a self-contained component that can be written in any supported framework and hydrated independently using one of three strategies: hydrate="load" — Hydrate immediately when the page loads (eager). hydrate="idle" — Hydrate when the browser is idle via requestIdleCallback. Show 1 more hydrate="visible" — Hydrate when the island scrolls into the viewport via IntersectionObserver.

sections.heading: What This Example Shows
sections.text: Multi-framework islands — React, Svelte, Vue, and Angular counter components all coexist on the same page, each hydrated independently. Shared cross-framework state — A shared counter store (counterIslandStore) built with createIslandStore allows all islands, regardless of framework, to read and write shared state. Typed islands — A central island registry provides full TypeScript type inference for framework, component name, and props when using TypedReactIsland, TypedSvelteIsland, TypedVueIsland, or TypedAngularIsland. Show 3 more Loose islands — The untyped <Island> primitive allows ad-hoc usage without the registry for quick prototyping. Multiple host pages — The same islands render from host pages written in React (/), Vue (/vue), Svelte (/svelte), Angular (/angular), plain HTML (/html), and HTMX (/htmx). Elysia server — The backend uses Elysia with the AbsoluteJS plugin for SSR, asset serving, and routing.

sections.heading: absolutejs-isolated-jsc-example
sections.text: absolutejs-isolated-jsc-example v0.0.1 beta Dev Tools Live demo of @absolutejs/isolated-jsc, a Bun-native sandbox for executing untrusted JavaScript with heap isolation, CPU timeouts, memory caps, brokered host capabilities, execution receipts, output limits, and an FFI backend when JavaScriptCore is available.

sections.heading: Installation
sections.text: BASH # Private workspace project: ~/abs/examples/isolated-jsc

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Live demo of @absolutejs/isolated-jsc, a Bun-native sandbox for executing untrusted JavaScript with heap isolation, CPU timeouts, memory caps, brokered host capabilities, execution receipts, output limits, and an FFI backend when JavaScriptCore is available. Paste code on the left, hit Run, see the result and any host-captured log calls on the right. The canned presets each demonstrate one isolation guarantee: Hello world — calls the host-injected log Reference; output streams back to the host. Show 9 more Host clock via Reference — calls a host-defined now() function from inside the sandbox. Runaway loop -> TimeoutError — tight while (true) {}; the host enforces the configured timeout. Memory bomb -> MemoryLimitError — allocates heap-resident JS objects past the configured cap; the isolate terminates. No host filesystem access — shows the hardened default global shape: host capability globals are not exposed directly. Result limit -> ResultSizeError — returns a payload larger than maxResultBytes; the host rejects it before app code accepts it. Capability output limit -> CapabilityError — asks a host capability to return more than its maxOutputBytes; the broker rejects it before sandbox code receives the value. Console limit -> receipt flag — emits more console lines than the host forwards; the receipt records truncation. Audit buffer -> receipt flag — calls a host capability repeatedly; the receipt records dropped audit events instead of retaining an unbounded array. Policy recipe helpers — shows the helper-built audit, broker, console, run, and runner options that wrap the sandbox request.

sections.heading: Run it
sections.text: Open whatever port the dev server prints (defaults to :3000, override with PORT=3100 bun run dev).

sections.heading: How it works
sections.text: src/backend/sandbox.ts — the POST /api/run endpoint. Each request uses runIsolated() with the tenant-script policy, exposes log and now through a typed capability broker, applies timeout/memory/result/console/audit limits through the policy recipe helper builders, and returns the result, helper-built recipe options, manifest, redacted audit events, receipt, backend metrics, and captured logs. The demo pins backend: "worker" so console capture is visible on every machine; production hostile-code paths should prefer FFI where JavaScriptCore is installed. src/backend/server.ts — wires the sandbox plugin into Elysia. src/frontend/react/pages/SandboxPage.tsx — single-page UI: source editor, memory/timeout inputs, result panel. Show 1 more The example deliberately uses one-shot execution to keep each demo self-contained. A real PaaS should use createIsolatedRunner() to pool by tenant/session, precompile hot callables, and expose host powers through typed capability tools with manifests and receipts.

sections.heading: Backend decision guide
sections.text: Use backend: "auto" for this demo, local development, and CI. It uses FFI when libJSC is reachable and falls back to Worker when it is not. Use backend: "ffi" for production hostile-code paths on macOS/Linux where JavaScriptCore is installed. FFI has lower cold heap, interrupt-driven timeouts, survives timeouts, and closes eval / Function-constructor residuals. If you must run arbitrary third-party code on the Worker fallback, add process/container isolation and keep host secrets, filesystem permissions, and network egress out of reach. Show 1 more For user plugins or agent tools, expose only explicit host capabilities, validate inputs, redact audited values, bound audit buffers, set timeouts, and audit every call.

sections.heading: Related examples
sections.text: /abs/examples/sync shows the application surface where sandboxed per-tenant mutation handlers matter. It keeps handlers in-process for clarity, but the hosted path should run customer-authored handlers through @absolutejs/isolated-jsc. The package repo example, bun run example:agent-tool in /abs/isolated-jsc, shows typed capability tools, tenant context, audit events, and per-call metrics. Outcomes

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: An example project demonstrating the AbsoluteJS out-of-order streaming model across React, Svelte, Vue, and Angular.

sections.heading: What Is Out-of-Order Streaming?
sections.text: Out-of-order streaming lets slow async sections stream as soon as they resolve instead of blocking everything above them in the response. Fast content arrives first, then slower stream slots patch in independently.

sections.heading: What This Example Shows
sections.text: Per-framework streaming pages - A dedicated route for each framework that uses StreamSlot. Fallback while waiting - Async chunks render with placeholders while work is still pending. Out-of-order delivery - Streamed slots resolve independently and patch in by slot ID. Show 2 more Cross-framework routing - One backend plugin drives React, Svelte, Vue, Angular, HTML, and HTMX routes. Shared example architecture - The app follows the same multi-framework example pattern used across the other AbsoluteJS example repositories.

sections.heading: How It Works
sections.text: Each streaming page renders fast shell content immediately, then defers slower sections into independently resolving stream slots. When a section finishes, AbsoluteJS patches that slot into the response without waiting for the rest of the page. This repository includes equivalent examples for React, Vue, Svelte, and Angular, plus plain HTML and HTMX reference routes for comparison.

An in-process worker drains a typed job queue; every page — React, Vue, Svelte, Angular, HTML, or HTMX — enqueues work and polls the live status as the worker picks jobs up, retries the occasional transient failure, and marks them done.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.text: Server (src/backend/queue.ts): defineJobs() declares the typed job kinds and createJobRegistry() registers their handlers. The queue Elysia plugin mounts the in-process worker (auto-starts) and decorates the context with queue.enqueue. POST /api/enqueue adds a demo.task, and GET /api/jobs returns the current job list plus per-status counts. The handler simulates work and occasionally fails the first attempt so the queue's automatic retry is visible. Client: every framework fetches GET /api/jobs on mount and polls it once Show 1 more a second, wiring an "Enqueue job" button to POST /api/enqueue and rendering the live stats + job list.

sections.text: absolutejs-spa-example v0.0.1 beta Dev Tools Demonstrates intra-framework SPA navigation in AbsoluteJS using each framework's native router. The top-level route between frameworks (/react → /svelte) is a full-page MPA navigation. The sub-routes inside each framework page (/react/settings, /react/profile) are client-side SPA navigations driven by the framework's own router.

sections.heading: Installation
sections.text: BASH # Private workspace project: ~/abs/examples/spa

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Demonstrates intra-framework SPA navigation in AbsoluteJS using each framework's native router. The top-level route between frameworks (/react → /svelte) is a full-page MPA navigation. The sub-routes inside each framework page (/react/settings, /react/profile) are client-side SPA navigations driven by the framework's own router. The point: AbsoluteJS doesn't ship a router. Users install react-router-dom / vue-router / svelte-routing themselves; the adapter just makes the SSR pass cooperate so SEO, deep-link load, and refresh-mid-route all work.

sections.heading: Run
sections.text: bun install bun run dev Open .

sections.heading: What to look at
sections.text: src/frontend/{react,svelte,vue,angular}/pages/ — each framework's SPA page wires its native router. Refreshing on a sub-route renders the correct view because the request URL is forwarded to the router on the server. src/backend/plugins/pagesPlugin.ts — Elysia routes use wildcard Show 9 more patterns (/react/ etc.) so the same handler responds for every sub-URL. React uses <StaticRouter location={url}> on the server and <BrowserRouter> on the client. URL is plumbed as a normal prop. Svelte uses <Router url={url}> from svelte-routing. URL is plumbed as a normal prop. Angular uses provideRouter exported from the page module. AbsoluteJS forwards request.url into renderApplication. Vue exports a setupApp(app, { url, isServer }) hook from the page module. AbsoluteJS calls this on both server and client, so app.use(router) + router.push(url) + router.isReady() runs in both environments.

sections.heading: Note on the Vue adapter
sections.text: The Vue setupApp convention is new in @absolutejs/absolute@0.19.0-beta.817. Page modules export setupApp(app, { url, isServer }); AbsoluteJS calls it on both server (in pageHandler.ts, before renderToWebStream) and client (in compileVue.ts's auto-generated index, before app.mount()). This is the only way to get vue-router cooperating with SSR + hydration without forking the Vue mount path. Outcomes

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The @absolutejs/sync Tier 3 sync engine, shown across every framework AbsoluteJS supports. A shared task list is a live collection: each page hydrates once over a WebSocket, then the server pushes { added, removed, changed } diffs — no polling. Edits apply optimistically and reconcile when the server confirms. Open two tabs (or two frameworks) and every open client stays in sync.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.text: Server (src/backend/sync.ts): createSyncEngine() registers a tasks collection and addTask/toggleTask/removeTask mutations, exposed over one Elysia WebSocket via syncSocket at /sync/ws. A mutation writes the in-memory store and emits the row change; the engine turns it into a diff for every subscriber. Client — one idiomatic binding per framework, all over the same socket: Show 7 more React (/): useSyncCollection from @absolutejs/sync/react Vue (/vue): useSyncCollection from @absolutejs/sync/vue Svelte (/svelte): createSyncCollectionStore from @absolutejs/sync/svelte Angular (/angular): SyncCollectionService from @absolutejs/sync/angular HTML & HTMX (/html, /htmx): a native WebSocket speaking the engine's frame protocol directly — no framework runtime needed. All of them return the same { data, status, error, mutate } and open the socket on the client only (SSR-safe).

sections.heading: Sandboxed handlers
sections.text: This example keeps mutation handlers in-process so the sync surfaces are easy to inspect. For customer-authored mutations, AI-generated transforms, or plugin code, install @absolutejs/isolated-jsc@0.8.0 and use sync's sandboxedHandler; the engine now routes those handlers through isolated-jsc's createIsolatedRunner() + tenant-script policy instead of calling them directly in the app process. Use backend: "ffi" for hostile-code production paths on macOS/Linux where JavaScriptCore is available. Use backend: "auto" for local development, CI, and demos so the Worker fallback keeps the example portable. Show 3 more If you must rely on the Worker fallback for arbitrary third-party code, add process/container isolation and avoid sharing host secrets or broad network/file permissions. Expose host powers through narrow actions. bridges: validate inputs, set timeouts, and audit calls. The hosted AbsoluteJS sync path uses this shape for sandboxed per-tenant mutation handlers; this example stays unsandboxed to keep the framework bindings and reactive collections front and center.

sections.heading: Run
sections.text: Open and a second tab on /vue (or any framework). Add, toggle, or delete a task in one — they all update together.

sections.text: absolutejs-voice-example v0.0.1 beta Dev Tools This is a full AbsoluteJS demo app for @absolutejs/voice.

sections.heading: Installation
sections.text: BASH # Private workspace project: ~/abs/examples/voice

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: This is a full AbsoluteJS demo app for @absolutejs/voice. It exposes the same voice intake flow across: React Show 10 more Vue Svelte Angular HTML HTMX The server uses: @absolutejs/voice for the WebSocket voice route @absolutejs/voice-deepgram with Deepgram Flux for STT @absolutejs/voice-assemblyai as an optional STT fallback provider route-level phraseHints

sections.heading: Run
sections.text: ASSEMBLYAI_API_KEY is optional. When present, the backend keeps Deepgram as the primary realtime STT provider and routes to AssemblyAI when Deepgram open/send fails, times out, or is temporarily suppressed by provider health. Optional LLM routing: Provider selection is automatic in this order: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, then deterministic fallback. You can force one with VOICE_MODEL_PROVIDER=openai, VOICE_MODEL_PROVIDER=anthropic, VOICE_MODEL_PROVIDER=gemini, or VOICE_MODEL_PROVIDER=deterministic. Show 10 more Provider model env vars are optional. If no LLM key is present, the server keeps using the deterministic local intake model so the demo still runs with only the voice/STT key. Then open: http://localhost:3000/react http://localhost:3000/vue http://localhost:3000/svelte http://localhost:3000/angular http://localhost:3000/html http://localhost:3000/htmx http://localhost:3000/reviews http://localhost:3000/assistant

sections.heading: Recommended Pattern
sections.text: The example now follows the same production pattern recommended in @absolutejs/voice itself: durable runtime storage via createVoiceFileRuntimeStorage(...) one assistant surface via createVoiceAssistant(...) Show 10 more provider-neutral model selection through createOpenAIVoiceAssistantModel(...), createAnthropicVoiceAssistantModel(...), and createGeminiVoiceAssistantModel(...) recipe-driven ops defaults via the assistant support-triage artifact plan voice({ ops: assistant.ops, onTurn: assistant.onTurn }) to record: reviews follow-up tasks integration events assistant run analytics from trace events thin app-specific customization through assistant guardrails, experiments, and model logic The persisted runtime data lives under: .voice-runtime/voice-demo/sessions

sections.heading: Provider Routing And Failover
sections.text: Every framework page includes the same provider selector. The selected provider is sent to the voice route as ?provider=openai, ?provider=anthropic, ?provider=gemini, or ?provider=deterministic. The backend routes every assistant turn through createVoiceProviderRouter(...) from @absolutejs/voice: prefer-selected keeps the user-selected provider first. Show 10 more configured fallback order is OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, then deterministic. adaptive provider health suppresses providers after provider errors or rate limits. rate-limit suppressions cool down for 120 seconds in this demo. successful recovery retries clear active suppression while preserving historical error counts. Provider status is visible in /assistant and /api/provider-status. Provider contract readiness is visible in /provider-contracts and /api/provider-contracts. The backend uses the package-level createVoiceProviderContractMatrixPreset("phone-agent", ...) primitive to turn the configured LLM, STT, and TTS providers into one deploy-checkable matrix: That one primitive proves configured state, required env, declared capabilities, streaming support, fallback coverage, and latency budgets without depending on a hosted dashboard. Status meanings: healthy: the provider has a successful recent run and is eligible. suppressed: the provider is temporarily skipped by the router; suppressionRemainingMs shows the cooldown.

sections.heading: What To Demo
sections.text: A good end-to-end demo flow is: Open /demo-checklist for the canonical presentation path. Open /switching-from-vapi when the buyer asks how Vapi dashboard concepts map to AbsoluteJS-owned primitives and proof URLs. Show 10 more Open any framework page. Complete a guided or general voice flow. sections.heading: Delivery Sinks
sections.text: Open /delivery-sinks to inspect the delivery primitive. The demo writes runtime trace exports into runtimeStorage.traceDeliveries and writes audit evidence for those exports into runtimeStorage.auditDeliveries. Production readiness consumes those same stores, so the UI proves export health without caring whether the sink is file-backed, webhook-backed, S3-backed, SQLite-backed, or Postgres-backed. Set VOICE_DELIVERY_SINK=file|webhook|s3|postgres|sqlite to change the sink descriptors shown in /delivery-sinks, /ops-console, and /production-readiness. In webhook and s3 modes, the drain endpoints use createVoiceDeliveryRuntimePresetConfig plus createVoiceDeliveryRuntime from the package: VOICE_DELIVERY_WEBHOOK_URL receives signed JSON envelopes, and VOICE_DELIVERY_S3_BUCKET=s3://bucket/prefix writes audit/trace JSON objects through Bun's native S3 client. Open /delivery-runtime for the package-level worker control plane. It shows audit and trace queue summaries and exposes one manual tick action for both delivery workers. Show 6 more The current example uses file-backed stores for local demos and mounts: /audit/deliveries /traces/deliveries /api/voice-audit-deliveries/drain /api/voice-trace-deliveries/drain Swap the store/worker layer to actually deliver to external infrastructure; keep the voice flow, descriptor, and readiness wiring the same.

sections.heading: Execution
sections.text: @absolutejs/execution v0.14.12 beta AI Crash-safe external effect execution for AI agents with a transactional outbox, queue integration, reconciliation, and compensation.

sections.heading: Installation
sections.text: BASH bun add @absolutejs/execution

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Crash-safe external effects for AI agents. Execution separates an agent's durable intent from the fallible provider call that fulfills it. The production path is PostgreSQL-first and reuses AbsoluteJS Queue: store.enqueue(effect) atomically inserts the effect and an outbox event. Show 10 more createExecutionOutboxDispatcher() idempotently moves that event into an @absolutejs/queue store (use @absolutejs/queue-postgres in production). Queue owns scheduling, worker leases, retries, backoff, and dead letters. createExecutionQueueHandler() owns provider idempotency, attempt history, results, unknown-outcome quarantine, and reconciliation. Redis is not required. A process crash before outbox publish leaves the event claimable; a crash after queue enqueue is harmless because the event id is also the queue idempotency key. ExecutionSqlClient accepts serialized JSON values as ordinary query parameters. Execution explicitly parses those values through PostgreSQL text before converting them to jsonb, so adapters for Bun SQL, postgres.js, and Neon must pass the provided values through unchanged rather than JSON-encoding them again. If a provider times out after accepting a request, throw UnknownEffectOutcomeError. Execution will not retry blindly: it quarantines the effect as unknown until an authorized operator, provider query, or provider webhook resolves it through createEffectRecoveryOperations(). Recovery verifies evidence before one atomic status transition, retains an append-only actor/source/evidence record, tenant-fences every case, and permits retry only when evidence confirms the provider did not apply the effect. That transition atomically creates a reconciliation-scoped outbox event so Queue can actually schedule the safe retry after the original event was consumed. Apply effectRecoveryPostgresSchemaSql() before using the PostgreSQL recovery API. Successful effects can be reversed explicitly with compensateEffect() when the handler provides compensate. Verified provider webhooks and query results can enter recovery through createEffectEvidenceIngestion(). The ingestion boundary retains only normalized, tenant-bound evidence, authorizes that binding before persistence, deduplicates provider delivery IDs, rejects attempts to rebind an existing delivery to another effect, and resumes reconciliation when a provider retries after a host crash. Production hosts should apply effectEvidencePostgresSchemaSql() and use createPostgresEffectEvidenceStore(). Raw webhook payloads and provider credentials do not belong in the evidence store. Agent Runtime hosts should use createAgentRuntimeEffectExecutor() rather than returning an enqueue result as if it were a completed effect. The bridge stores one tenant/run-fenced effect and asks Runtime to wait until the queue handler records a terminal result. Its authorize callback must return the exact Agency action ID and input digest retained for execution-time lease issuance.

sections.heading: Certified adapters and tenant installations
sections.text: createEffectAdapterRegistry() is the global fail-closed boundary. Adapter descriptors declare effects, destinations, credential slots, idempotency, reconciliation, compensation, and spend authority. Activation requires a fresh certificate for the exact descriptor digest and host-verified evidence. Webhook reconciliation descriptors must also declare their relative {tenantId} callback template, raw-body signature headers, project secret alias, provider event set, health signal, and replacement or overlap rotation behavior. Query reconciliation descriptors bind their provider query to a declared credential slot and declare outcomes, polling cadence, health freshness, and rotation verification. Registration rejects incomplete or unsafe setup, and effectAdapterWebhookCallbackPath() renders a tenant-safe callback without provider-specific host branching. createEffectAdapterReconciliationRuntime() scans quarantined effects and claims a durable per-effect lease before any provider query. It authorizes the tenant installation before resolving the exact credential alias, gives query drivers only effect identity metadata rather than the original payload, and passes normalized evidence back through createEffectEvidenceIngestion(). Use createPostgresEffectReconciliationLeaseStore() and createPostgresEffectAdapterHealthStore() after applying effectAdapterReconciliationPostgresSchemaSql(). Health is a bounded upserted signal containing safe codes and counters; raw provider errors and credentials are never retained. Operator-triggered owner flows must call runOnce({ tenantId }); the tenant filter is passed into the durable effect inventory before any lease, installation authorization, credential resolution, or provider query occurs. Adapters that use a signed webhook as the primary path and a provider query as a fallback declare mode: "webhook-query". Query contracts explicitly state whether a provider reference is required. An execution driver may extract only the bounded { provider, resourceId } reference from a successful provider result; Execution adds the certified adapter ID and never exposes the arbitrary result or original payload to a query driver. If local completion loses its lease, quarantineUnknown() compares the exact attempt number before retaining that reference. A stale worker therefore cannot overwrite a newer attempt or a terminal effect. Fallbacks that require a reference are skipped before credential resolution when an ambiguous provider call never returned one. Show 5 more createManagedEffectReconciliationScheduler() adds a durable, explicitly default-off control-plane schedule around that runtime. Its store retains the interval, next run, replica lease, bounded counters, and a safe error code. A policy survives restarts, and initialize() never overwrites an operator's existing choice. Use createPostgresEffectReconciliationSchedulerStore() after applying effectReconciliationSchedulerPostgresSchemaSql(). The local polling loop may run on every replica because only the durable due claim can start a reconciliation pass. createEffectAdapterInstallationRegistry() narrows that certified authority for one tenant. Every installation pins the adapter version and digest, starts disabled, selects an effect and destination subset, maps required adapter credential slots to host-owned secret aliases without storing values, and can bind a per-effect spend ceiling to a mandate. Enabling and every authorization recheck the global adapter, descriptor pin, credential aliases, mandate, destination, effect, tenant, and spend ceiling. Descriptor drift or revoked evidence therefore stops every dependent installation without a rollout. Production hosts should apply effectAdapterRegistryPostgresSchemaSql() and effectAdapterInstallationsPostgresSchemaSql(), then use the corresponding PostgreSQL stores. The host callbacks remain responsible for resolving secret aliases and validating mandates; raw credentials never enter either registry. createEffectAdapterExecutionHandler() is the final provider boundary. It accepts an installation envelope, reauthorizes the exact tenant, effect, destination, and spend, first recomputes the canonical authorized input digest, verifies that the runtime driver's identity, version, idempotency, reconciliation, and compensation capabilities match the certified descriptor, and only then resolves the authorized secret aliases. Credential values exist only in the driver context and are never placed in the durable installation record or bridge result. Unknown provider outcomes should be raised as UnknownEffectOutcomeError so the queue quarantines them for reconciliation instead of retrying an ambiguous side effect. When an authorized envelope carries positive spend, the bridge requires a settlement callback and runs it only after provider success, before returning a successful effect result. The normalized result retains the mandate, currency, and amount needed for a post-compensation refund without retaining credentials. Spending envelopes carry that same mandate and currency explicitly, so an unknown effect retains its original settlement authority even if installation policy changes before provider evidence arrives. The mandate's spend binding is the canonical durable effect-input digest. Confirmed-success webhook, provider-query, and operator reconciliation paths also require settlement before making an unknown effect terminal. Settlement and refund callbacks must be idempotent under the effect identity so a crash at either boundary can be retried safely.

sections.heading: Bounded background steps
sections.text: runCheckpointedSteps runs an immutable finite plan under a caller-owned, renewed execution lease. Its adapter must atomically save the full checkpoint using the expected revision. Save a unique plan key that covers every execution input. Completed steps are reused. An in-flight marker on recovery throws UnknownEffectOutcomeError: do not retry that provider operation blindly. Return from runStep only after known usage writes drain. A false beforeStep result durably stops the plan (for example, at the agreed credit ceiling). createExecutionQueueHandler renews its effect lease (30 seconds by default, renewed every 10 seconds), forwards shutdown/lease loss through the handler's signal, and quarantines uncertain completion. Each invocation has a unique lease owner. The queue job lease must also exceed the bounded job duration or be renewed by the queue worker. This API does not make arbitrary providers idempotent. Resumable funding pauses Show 1 more Return { pause: "funding" } from runCheckpointedSteps.beforeStep to persist a resumable stop before the next provider call. After funding is verified and an exclusive execution lease is acquired, pass resume: { expectedRevision, reason: "funding" }. The runner checks the exact checkpoint revision, immutable plan and pause reason, preserves completed results, and rejects any in-flight uncertain operation. A plain false remains a terminal stop. Never reset a checkpoint or create a new plan just to retry a funding interruption.

sections.heading: Effect state machine
sections.text: Execution distinguishes known failure from unknown provider outcomes so retries cannot duplicate consequential effects. Intent Bind the exact authorized effect and idempotency identity. Outbox Persist work before publishing it to a worker. Lease Acquire a fenced execution lease. Execute Perform the provider action and capture raw evidence. Unknown Quarantine timeouts or ambiguous responses. Resolve Reconcile, settle, retry safely, or compensate. Outcomes

sections.heading: Geometry
sections.text: @absolutejs/geometry v0.18.0 beta Frontend & UX Bounded geometry projection, oriented material components, point membership and plane-clipped volume and surface moments for web 3D tooling.

sections.heading: Installation
sections.text: BASH bun add @absolutejs/geometry

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Worker-side measurement of alpha-masked triangle geometry. The first API measures orthographic coverage without Three.js, a renderer, or a GPU. This is useful for asset inspection, canopy gap measurement, and tools in a 3D website builder.

sections.heading: Coordinate and texture contract
sections.text: Positions are xyz in the caller's projection frame, projected onto xz. Supply transformed positions for the actual pose, preferably in local double precision. An origin already rounded away in Float32 cannot be recovered. Indexed vertices define a convex reference hull; its area includes transparent card extents and gaps between disconnected leaves. This is a declared reference footprint, not a botanical crown boundary. Units are caller-defined; areas use squared units. UVs must already include any texture transform. Alpha is row-major, one byte per texel, with v=0 at the first row: apply any image flip before calling. Bilinear sampling uses the base texture level, wrapS/wrapT default to clamp, and alpha at or above cutoff is covered. Repeat and mirrored repeat are supported. Faces are two-sided; overlapping faces form a union. No color-space conversion applies to alpha. Material opacity, vertex alpha, multiple materials and blend materials must be resolved by the caller; this API does not silently approximate them.

sections.heading: Results and accuracy
sections.text: cells is a resolution-squared mask: 0 outside the reference hull, 1 open, 2 covered. Rows run from minZ to maxZ; columns from minX to maxX. bounds is [minX, minZ, maxX, maxZ]. footprintArea is the analytic hull area; sampledFootprintArea and sampledCoveredArea expose center-sampling error. coveredArea normalizes the sampled coverage fraction to the analytic hull. gapFraction is the open fraction of sampled hull cells. Center sampling can miss thin geometry and small holes. Compare resolutions for your asset; convergence is evidence, not a rigorous error bound. The game asset audit in docs covers all eight canonical trees plus deformed and fallen examples. This does not measure light transmission, rainfall interception, storage capacity, wind deformation, mip-filtered screen coverage, or hydrologic history.

sections.heading: Cost and ownership
sections.text: Run this synchronous function in a worker or an offline asset pipeline, never a render loop. It does not mutate input buffers. Transfer owned copies when worker ownership must change; do not detach a renderer's borrowed geometry buffers. Limits: 300,000 vertices, 200,000 triangles, 4,194,304 texture texels, resolution 8–1024, finite UV magnitudes at most 1,000,000. Triangle-local bounding rectangles are charged against maxPixelTests (default 50 million, maximum 100 million) before rasterization. The counter is conservative even when union early-outs skip already covered cells. Hull construction sorts indexed vertices; scanline setup walks convex hull edges. These limits bound work and allocation, not wall time. Worker owners should additionally enforce deadlines and cancellation. Malformed, unresolved, degenerate and over-budget inputs throw.

sections.heading: Development
sections.text: BVM selects Bun 1.4.4+absolute.1 from .bun-version. Run bun install --frozen-lockfile and bun run check:package. bun scripts/audit-game-canopies.ts additionally requires the Hello World checkout and its development asset tooling; see docs/canopy-audit/README.md. Licensed under BSL-1.1; see LICENSE for the additional use grant and change date.

sections.heading: Worker-side alpha preparation (0.1.1)
sections.text: alphaFromRgba(rgba, width, height) copies one alpha byte per RGBA8 texel into an owned Uint8Array. It accepts Uint8Array or Uint8ClampedArray and validates the exact byte length and the same 4,194,304-texel budget before allocation. alphaFromImageBitmap(bitmap) reads an already decoded bitmap using a temporary OffscreenCanvas 2D context with willReadFrequently: true. Call it in a worker; it performs synchronous CPU readback wherever it is called. The temporary canvas is released afterward. It does not create a WebGL context, close the input bitmap, or detach any borrowed renderer resource. The caller owns bitmap cleanup. Unsupported runtimes, closed/invalid bitmaps and oversized images fail explicitly. There is no hidden main-thread fallback. ImageBitmap supports structured cloning as well as transfer. The browser-worker qualification checks exact alpha values and that closing a cloned worker image leaves its source usable. Transfer only owned copies if using a transfer list. See the HTML ImageBitmap ownership contract and OffscreenCanvas. These helpers prepare raster inputs; they do not assign hydrologic meaning to alpha.

sections.heading: Oriented solid boundaries (0.2.0)
sections.text: closedComponents(positions, indices) splits index-connected closed oriented boundary shells. Coincident coordinates never weld distinct authored vertices. solidPointMembership(positions, indices) prepares a solid-angle classifier that returns inside, outside, or boundary; oriented cavity walls cancel their outer shell's winding inside a void. solidComponents(positions, indices, faceOwners, maxTriangleTests?) returns { components, shells, cavities, pointQueries, triangleTests }. Each component contains positions, indices and original sourceTriangles. It preserves separate positive components of the same source, and assigns each inward cavity to the smallest enclosing positive shell of its explicitly declared source. It never infers source identity, takes absolute cavity mass, or uses a convex hull. Precondition: each owner's input must be a valid, nonintersecting oriented solid boundary, such as a validated Boolean kernel result. Shells must not touch. Topology checks and all-cavity-vertex containment checks are not a complete triangle-intersection validator; do not use this API to repair arbitrary soups. An outward material island inside an inward cavity remains a separate component. Deterministic order is positive-shell order, followed by each component's cavity shells; provenance follows that same face order (not globally sorted). Show 2 more Inputs are Float64 positions, Uint32 indices, and Int16/Uint16 per-face owners. Limits: 100,000 vertices, 200,000 triangles, 128 shells. Prepared point classifiers support up to 20,000 triangles; containment charges every tested outer triangle per cavity vertex, with 2 million tests by default (maximum 8 million). No GPU, Three.js, WASM, or runtime dependencies. All coordinates must share one local frame; point boundary tolerance is 1e-7 coordinate units, winding tolerance 1e-5. Near-degenerate faces, unresolved orientation, missing cavity parents, detected touching/crossing shells and exhausted budgets throw rather than guess. Sources: Manifold's oriented boundary representation and Jacobson et al.'s generalized winding numbers.

sections.heading: Initial material overlap audit (0.3.0)
sections.text: auditSolidOverlaps(meshes, kernel, maximumQueries = 256) checks solid intersection volumes before physics publication. Supply {create(mesh), intersect(a,b)} using your Boolean backend. Handles implement volume() and delete(); each operation must return a new owned handle. A factory that throws must release any allocation it made before throwing. The audit releases all successfully returned handles on both success and failure, and passes private position/index copies to the kernel. No Boolean engine is bundled or required at runtime. The result includes per-mesh oriented volumes, pair indices/intersection volumes, fraction of the smaller solid, query count, bounds skips and maximum input volume round-trip error. Touching/disjoint bounds need no native intersection. Candidate pairs are rebased before construction. Native volume error above 1e-5 or impossible intersection volume rejects; tiny nonzero intersections are reported, not rounded away. The host chooses its material-resolution threshold explicitly. Use valid oriented material boundaries, including cavity walls. The API does not repair overlapping shells within one input mesh, assign source ownership, union models, predict extraction clearance or validate dynamic contact penetration. Bounds are not proof of overlap. Limits: 64 meshes, 100,000 total vertices, 200,000 total triangles, and at most 1,024 requested pair queries. A host worker must impose its own lifetime bound on its injected native kernel.

sections.heading: Exclusive material partition (0.4.0)
sections.text: partitionSolidMaterials(meshes, kernel, maximumOperations = 126) implements ordered solid ownership. Cell i is input i minus the union of earlier inputs. The caller explicitly chooses the order; this library does not invent a material priority. Inputs must be valid oriented solid boundaries, including cavity walls. Supply {create(mesh), subtract(a,b), union(a,b), mesh(solid)}. Native handles implement volume() and delete(); every construction/operation returns a fresh handle, and failures inside the adapter must clean up allocations not returned. mesh returns Float64 positions and Uint32 indices in the supplied local frame. Return a valid closed boundary, or two empty arrays for an empty solid. The package copies all borrowed arrays and releases native handles on success/failure. At most three native handles are retained at once, including the output of the current operation; previous union/intermediate geometry is promptly released. Results include: Show 8 more cells: one entry per input, with stable source index, mesh and volume. A fully covered source remains an explicitly empty cell. exterior: the separate whole-union boundary and volume. inputVolumes, authoredVolume, materialVolume, volumeDifference, maximumVolumeError and operations. The signed volume difference is not clamped; insignificant negative roundoff can remain. Cell walls include internal material interfaces. Do not render every cell wall as exposed material or infer that two touching cells are detached. Exterior face provenance, adjacency, strength, density, fracture surfaces and extraction/physics acceptance remain host concerns. In particular this does not turn an existing positive-overlap attachment graph into a surface-interface graph. Limits: 1–64 inputs, 100,000 input vertices/200,000 input triangles, up to 126 Boolean operations, and 200,000 exported vertices/400,000 exported triangles across all cells plus exterior. Native input/output volume and total conservation errors above 1e-5 reject. These are acceptance budgets, not certified geometric error bounds or a proof against a faulty Boolean backend. Topology checks do not detect all geometric self-intersections. Use a cancellable worker: a synchronous backend call cannot be interrupted by an operation counter. The implementation uses the set identity C_i = S_i ∖ (S_0 ∪ … ∪ S_(i−1)); its tests use Manifold only as a development dependency. Manifold's documentation describes the native Boolean/volume contract. No Boolean engine is bundled.

sections.heading: Boundary ancestry and optional Manifold adapter (0.5.0)
sections.headingTerms: boundary ancestry and optional manifold adapter (0.5.0)
sections.text: Partition kernels receive create(mesh, sourceIndex). Their mesh(solid) can return origins: {sources: Uint16Array, faces: Uint32Array, reversed: Uint8Array}, one entry per output triangle. These identify a source mesh/triangle and whether subtraction exposed its backside. This is boundary ancestry, distinct from a cell's volume owner. The result copies and verifies this metadata; absent ancestry is explicitly null. auditSurfaceOrigins(mesh, origins, sourceMeshes, maximumPlaneDistance = 1e-6) checks every output vertex against its nominated source triangle and verifies winding. Invalid IDs, lengths, orientation, unrelated triangles and exhausted budgets throw. The plane-distance acceptance range is 1e-7 through 1e-5 in the input coordinate units; this is not a certified Boolean error bound. triangleWeights exports the same dominant-plane barycentric interpolation for material attributes, including thin triangles; it rejects off-surface points. mergeIndexedMesh(mesh, center, tolerance) reconstructs indexed geometry using an explicit merge map. It never welds nearby vertices by guessed distance. It accepts three Float32 position properties, Uint32 indices and merge arrays, checks finite coordinates/indices/merge displacement, and restores the supplied origin in double precision. This reconstructs topology; use the separate closed boundary/component validators where appropriate. Show 7 more For Manifold 3.5.1, the optional @absolutejs/geometry/manifold entry exports createManifoldPartitionKernel(wasm, sourceCount = 64). Pass your initialized module. The optional peer is not imported at runtime and the core entry point does not require Manifold. The adapter supplies create/subtract/union/intersect/export, native status checks, original mesh IDs, face IDs and backside flags. It creates fresh IDs for overlap operands when no explicit source index is given. Export now preserves native double-precision positions through getManifoldMesh64(solid), also exported from the optional Manifold entry. A temporary property channel stores exact integer indices into a bounded sidecar captured by Manifold's property callback; the final Float32 property index recovers the original double position. No simplification, proximity welding or tolerance change is used. The temporary native copy is freed. getManifoldMesh64 returns owned arrays with interleaved Float64 vertProperties, numProp, triangle indices, explicit merge maps, original IDs, face IDs, run boundaries and per-run reversed flags. Extra property values keep native getMesh export semantics (including transformed normals); only position precision is upgraded. The input solid remains owned and unchanged by the caller. The result is an export record, not an input accepted directly by Manifold's Float32 Mesh API. Limits:200,000 triangles,100,000 exported property vertices,16 extra channels, and at most600,000 position callbacks. mergeIndexedMesh accepts Float32 or Float64 position-only buffers and still uses explicit merge ancestry. Core imports remain independent of Manifold. createManifoldMesh64(wasm, mesh) imports a position-only mesh with numProp: 3, Float64 vertProperties, Uint32 triVerts, and optional native mesh metadata (such as face IDs and original source runs). The partition adapter uses this helper. It constructs the required Float32 native Mesh, then restores the exact original coordinates via native warp before Boolean operations. It rejects nonfinite coordinates, distinct doubles with the same rounded Float32 position, unknown native vertices, and changes to vertex/triangle counts during import or restoration. Input bounds are 100,000 vertices and 200,000 triangles. Intermediate native handles are released; callers own the returned solid. This does not recover coordinates already lost before this call, repair topology, certify self-intersection freedom, or guarantee every thin mesh can pass the native Float32 constructor. Rejections are explicit. Keep precision-sensitive operations native until final export when possible; repeated serialization/rebasing can still introduce slivers at coincident cut faces. The ancestry contract does not assign grain across a newly cut face spanning multiple materials, validate a collider, or prove a physical attachment.

sections.heading: Principal inertia frame
sections.text: principalInertiaFrame(tensor) accepts nine finite numbers containing a symmetric row-major inertia tensor, in any consistent mass/length units. It returns sorted positive principal moments and an {x,y,z,w} unit-quaternion frame mapping principal coordinates into the original coordinates. The bounded double-precision Jacobi solver checks symmetry, physical moment inequalities and reconstruction; it rejects invalid input rather than repairing it. Isotropic/repeated moments may have non-unique physical axes; the returned frame is deterministic for identical input, not a temporally continuous orientation for animations. Use the full tensor, including off-diagonal terms. This helper does not integrate mesh mass or validate collisions. When passing explicit mass properties to Rapier, set collision-shape density to zero to avoid adding their mass a second time; unit conversion remains the caller's responsibility. No physics engine is imported. Unoriented fibre mixtures Show 10 more axialOrientationTensor([{axis: [1, 0, 0], weight: 1}, ...]) returns the second orientation moment as a transferable row-major Float64Array. Directions are normalized and weights are nonnegative. An axis and its negation contribute identically, avoiding cancellation when blending wood, hair or textile fibre axes. All-zero weights, zero axes and invalid input fail explicitly; at most 4096 samples are accepted. Input arrays are never changed. Finite vector and weight scales near the limits of double precision are normalized before accumulation. The output is symmetric, positive semidefinite and has trace one. It intentionally does not choose a unique direction for isotropic or conflicting orientations. A second moment discards higher-order distribution information; it is neither a full fibre distribution nor a biological growth, fracture or constitutive model. Use a separate calibrated material model for strength and breaking forces. Thin-face membership uses scaled normals and dominant-plane projection. Nonzero faces are not rejected by an absolute area cutoff; exactly collinear boundary faces retain their edges. The existing 1e-7 boundary tolerance and winding checks remain unchanged. This does not make Boolean geometry exact below native feature limits, and does not alter source topology or repair degenerate whole solids. Plane-clipped tetrahedron moments tetrahedronPlaneMoments(vertices, planePoint, planeNormal) integrates the part of a four-vertex oriented tetrahedron on the side dot(position - planePoint, planeNormal) <= 0. The normal need not be unit length. It returns signed clipped/full volumes, their ratio, a centroid (null for an empty cut), a reference point and signed first moments relative to that reference. Input arrays are borrowed synchronously and never changed. No engine or native allocation is required; work is bounded by four faces and six crossed edges. Orientation matters: reversing two vertices reverses signed volume and moments. For a valid closed-solid tetrahedral decomposition, sum signed contributions; do not take each contribution's absolute value. To combine first moments with a common reference r, add firstMoment + signedVolume (reference - r). The helper does not construct or validate that decomposition. Tiny represented wet corners are retained using a shared cut-vertex integration origin, with no absolute volume cutoff. Degenerate or unrepresentable results throw; this is floating-point geometry, not exact predicates. A ratio can exceed one by accepted floating-point roundoff up to 1e-12; no silent clamping repairs the output. This measures geometry, not buoyancy or fluid response. A sealed air compartment and an open flooded cavity do not exclude the same water volume; the caller must supply the appropriate physical region. Water-surface curvature, density, force, torque, pressure dynamics and clock ownership are separate responsibilities. Prepared plane moments (0.11) For repeated cuts of an unchanged body-local tetrahedron, use prepareTetrahedronPlaneMoments(vertices) and call the returned function with (planePoint, planeNormal). Preparation owns a copy of the four vertices and caches plane-independent normalization and full moments. Each query returns the same signed-volume, centroid and relative-first-moment contract as tetrahedronPlaneMoments. Returned arrays can be changed without modifying later queries. Rebuild the prepared query when source geometry changes. For moving rigid bodies, transform the plane into body-local coordinates and transform the resulting centroid back. The package does not supply rigid-body forces, water clocks, sealing/flooding rules or a displacement-mesh validity certificate. Signed tetrahedral contributions must retain their orientation.

sections.heading: Exact zero-extent shell regularization
sections.text: regularizeZeroExtentShells(positions, indices) removes only complete disconnected closed shells whose coordinate range is exactly zero on at least one axis. Such shells have no 3D interior. There is no epsilon, near-flat test or volume cutoff; even subnormal nonzero thickness is retained. Non-axis-aligned flat geometry is also retained. This is a narrow certificate for coincident tool-plane artifacts, not general mesh repair or a complete regularized Boolean implementation. Results contain owned positions, indices, a retained sourceTriangles map, retainedShells, and removed certificates with axis, coordinate and original face indices. Topology must be closed before processing. Run it in the frame that makes the intended plane exact, before rotating or translating output for display.

sections.heading: Native cut sessions
sections.text: createManifoldCutSession(wasm, inputs, maximumCuts?) is available from the optional @absolutejs/geometry/manifold entry. Inputs and cutters are closed oriented meshes in one caller-chosen common frame. The session unions the inputs once and retains the native solid across cuts, avoiding a Float32 import of generated thin triangles between operations. It does not infer a tool frame or snap nearly shared planes. Each exported snapshot verifies face ancestry against owned source copies and reports exact zero-extent sheets separately. Failed edits leave the previous native state intact and release pending handles. Physical volume conservation must agree within 1e-8 relative to the pre-cut material. This is geometry acceptance, not collision, grain, canopy, motion or material-strength certification. Callers must keep the worker bounded and explicitly dispose sessions; rendering copies must not be treated as a lossless serialization of native session state. Limits: 1–63 initial sources, at most 32 accepted cuts, at most 64 total source IDs, 100,000 source vertices and 200,000 source triangles across all inputs/cutters, Show 4 more coordinate — ≤ 1000, and bounded native exports. Default cut budget is the smaller of 32 and the remaining source-ID capacity. Snapshot statistics expose native counts, volume/tolerance, exported triangles and removed sheet triangles for host diagnostics. No GPU or engine initialization is performed by this adapter. Double import now assigns a unique original face ID per triangle when IDs are omitted. Without this, the native Float32 constructor can merge rounded coplanar faces before restoration; immediate import volume can still match while a later cut changes. Explicit face IDs retain caller semantics. Disjoint or merely touching cutter bounds skip native splitting (broadPhaseSkipped). This remains allowed after the accepted-cut quota is full. Empty snapshots report nativeTolerance: null; skipped empty results report nativeEvaluated: false. No near-contact tolerance is introduced by this broad phase.

sections.heading: Read-only native coverage
sections.text: auditManifoldCoverage(wasm, target, candidates) from the Manifold entry, or session.auditCoverage(candidates), compares candidate cells with actual material components while retaining native target geometry. Results include owned target and component meshes, independent missing/excess volumes, measured cell intersections, cross-body overlap and bounded operation counts. Temporary native objects are always released; standalone callers retain ownership of target. Overlapping cells are unioned for coverage, so summed collider volume is not mistaken for physical mass. Cavity walls and nested islands remain separate material components. The API reports geometry evidence; it does not certify convexity, contacts or a game's acceptance policy. Bounds and qualification notes are in docs/native-coverage-2026-10-31/README.md.

sections.heading: Positive quadratic triangle moments
sections.text: prepareTrianglePositiveQuadraticMoments([a, b, c]) owns a finite, nondegenerate triangle and returns a query accepting three scalar values at its vertices. It integrates their affine interpolant s over the portion where s > 0: area, integral = ∫s² dA, cubicIntegral = ∫s³ dA, and relativeFirstMoment = ∫(x-reference)s² dA. meanOffset is the quadratic-weighted point relative to the owned reference, or null for zero pressure. The result also includes full area and the oriented unit surface normal. Returned arrays are owned; mutating them does not affect future queries. The query clips in triangle barycentric coordinates and integrates polynomial moments analytically. It does not subdivide into samples, call WASM, infer a drag coefficient, determine exposure to flow, or advance a body. Keeping moments in a relative frame avoids forming a weighted absolute position at large coordinates. Non-finite inputs, degenerate triangles and unrepresentable output powers throw. This is double-precision arithmetic, not an exact-arithmetic geometry kernel. An optional second query argument supplies three affine domain values. Integration then includes only points where both pressure scalar and domain scalar are positive. For a horizontal waterline, supply each vertex's depth below the surface as the domain value. This clips wet area exactly before computing the pressure moments; a fully dry domain yields zero moments. Domain boundaries carry no area, and a field that is identically zero is excluded. This remains a flat boundary calculation, not a wave or fluid solver. Show 1 more Closed-solid surface queries validate the plane once, then use an internal normalized-plane path for each triangle. Public triangle queries retain their input validation and owned results. Surface flux is accumulated with scalar coordinates to avoid temporary vectors; clipping rules, component ownership, precision guards and summation order are unchanged.

sections.heading: Positive linear triangle moments
sections.text: prepareTrianglePositiveLinearMoments([a, b, c]) owns the same validated triangle geometry and affine-domain clipping as the quadratic query. Its returned function accepts three finite field values and an optional three-value positive domain. It integrates the positive linear field: integral = integral(s dA) and relativeFirstMoment = integral((x-reference) s dA). meanOffset is the weighted point relative to reference, or null for a zero result. area, fullArea and oriented surfaceNormal are also returned. Every returned array is owned. There is no cubicIntegral on the linear result. For hydrostatic pressure, field values may be vertex depths below a waterline, with an explicitly supplied domain describing the exposed region. The math does not decide contact sealing, permeability or fluid connectivity. A caller can assemble force from -normal integral and torque from the first moment, with its own physical coefficient and reference-frame conversion. An all-zero domain is empty. Exactly opposed field/domain values are also empty: this is an exact identity at all three vertices, not an epsilon or volume cutoff. Nearby thin positive domains remain integrated. Nonfinite/unrepresentable results reject explicitly. Fully retained domains share the direct polynomial fast path; crossing domains retain analytic clipping without point sampling. Show 6 more Bounded surface domains (queued 0.17.0 extension) partitionTriangleAffineDomains(triangle, domains, options) partitions a triangle into convex polygons. Each domain is an intersection of affine fields supplied as three values at the input vertices; nonnegative values are inside. Returned reference, relativePositions, barycentric and domains arrays are owned by the result. Positions stay relative to the input triangle origin, avoiding collapse when a small partition sits at a large absolute coordinate. Retain the origin through downstream transforms; adding it prematurely can lose that precision. Domain indices describe each polygon's relative interior; zero-area boundary fragments are not separate cells. An identically zero field includes the full polygon. partitionTriangleBoxDomains supplies the six fields for each axis-aligned box. Use the barycentric coordinates for attribute interpolation and fan-triangulate each convex polygon. Defaults limit output to 1,024 cells and 8,192 vertices; explicit limits are checked during partitioning. Invalid input, unrepresentable intersections, area-conservation failure or exhausted budgets throw, without returning partial results. These are bounded double-precision operations, not exact-arithmetic Boolean solid repair. Domain membership is not a proof of solid ownership: applications must establish their own material/volume assumptions. For example, the triangle [[0,0,0],[1,0,0],[0,1,0]] and one domain [[[-0.5,0.5,0.5]]] separate the region x+y >= 0.5; its area is 0.375. A positive rescaling of the affine field describes the same domain. Repeated source-face interpolation prepareTriangleWeights(a, b, c, maximumPlaneDistance?) owns a prepared source triangle and returns a point-query function. Use it when multiple cut vertices share the same source face. It preserves dominant-plane projection, outside-face rejection and the existing projection-distance limits; each result is an owned three-element array. triangleWeights remains the one-shot form. Nonrepresentable geometry or query arithmetic rejects instead of returning nonfinite weights.

sections.heading: Repeated upward surface queries
sections.text: prepareUpwardSurface({ positions, indices, cellSize: 4 }) builds an owned XZ spatial index for upward-wound mesh faces. Positions are Float32Array or Float64Array xyz triples; indices are Uint16Array or Uint32Array triangle triples. Coordinates and heights must use the same frame and units. The game can reuse it for terrain support; builders can inspect walkable surfaces or place objects. The nearest upward surface is returned, not necessarily the highest surface. Downward ceilings and exactly vertical/degenerate projections are excluded. Equal-distance ties retain input triangle order. No height is extrapolated across missing coverage. maxDistance is inclusive; callers needing a strict threshold can apply it to the result. Optional fifth query argument edgeTolerance (default 1e-8, maximum 1e-4) controls dimensionless barycentric edge tolerance inside indexed cells; it does not expand the index's geometric footprint. Preparation retains no input buffers: they may be changed or transferred after preparation. .stats reports triangle/upward-face/cell/reference counts and coefficient bytes (not total JS/Map overhead). Each query reports actual indexed triangle visits. Inputs are capped at 262,144 vertices and 131,072 triangles; maxReferences defaults to 262,144 and cannot exceed 1,048,576. Grid reference expansion is checked before inserting a face, so an enormous face with tiny cells fails rather than silently causing unbounded work. Invalid inputs, unsafe grid coordinates and nonfinite arithmetic throw RangeError. Empty meshes are allowed. Show 1 more This module imports no renderer, React or physics engine. A support hit is not a solid-membership result, a contact manifold or proof that a body is balanced. Multiple chunks must be queried in their own coordinate frames; missing neighboring geometry remains unknown. Use repeated sample queries to build application-specific support policies rather than treating a single center hit as whole-object support. Outcomes

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Worker-side measurement of alpha-masked triangle geometry. The first API measures orthographic coverage without Three.js, a renderer, or a GPU. This is useful for asset inspection, canopy gap measurement, and tools in a 3D website builder.

sections.heading: Coordinate and texture contract
sections.text: Positions are xyz in the caller's projection frame, projected onto xz. Supply transformed positions for the actual pose, preferably in local double precision. An origin already rounded away in Float32 cannot be recovered. Indexed vertices define a convex reference hull; its area includes transparent card extents and gaps between disconnected leaves. This is a declared reference footprint, not a botanical crown boundary. Units are caller-defined; areas use squared units.

sections.heading: Results and accuracy
sections.text: cells is a resolution-squared mask: 0 outside the reference hull, 1 open, 2 covered. Rows run from minZ to maxZ; columns from minX to maxX. bounds is [minX, minZ, maxX, maxZ]. footprintArea is the analytic hull area; sampledFootprintArea and sampledCoveredArea expose center-sampling error. coveredArea normalizes the sampled coverage fraction to the analytic hull. gapFraction is the open fraction of sampled hull cells. sections.heading: Installation
sections.text: BASH bun add @absolutejs/git

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Authenticated Git source ingestion for Bun control planes and AbsoluteJS. The package turns a signed provider webhook into a normalized, authorized exact revision, checks that revision out without a shell, strips Git metadata, applies source-size and file-count limits, and emits portable provenance. It does not own credentials, databases, queues, build sandboxes, deployment, or UI. GitHub App installations can also create and update normalized Check Runs so a control plane reports exact-revision deployment posture without hand-writing provider payloads.

sections.heading: Security boundary
sections.text: Verify signatures against the untouched request bytes before parsing JSON. Derive canonical provider URLs instead of trusting webhook clone URLs. Authorize both repository identity and full ref before checkout. Show 8 more Fetch and verify the exact commit, never a moving branch tip. Pass Git arguments as an array; credentials use child-process environment configuration and are never embedded in repository URLs or errors. Remove .git, reject links and special files, and enforce source bounds before handing a tree to a build system. Run installation and builds in a separate sandbox with network, CPU, memory, time, and output limits. That policy belongs to the host control plane. @absolutejs/deploy/release-artifact remains the ecosystem owner of immutable deployment archives and their SHA-256 integrity contract. Outcomes

sections.heading: Handoff
sections.text: @absolutejs/handoff v0.1.0 beta AI Correlation, evidence, reconciliation, and visibility primitives for work handed to external systems.

sections.heading: Installation
sections.text: BASH bun add @absolutejs/handoff

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Storage-neutral correlation and evidence for work that leaves your application. A handoff starts in your code, continues in an external system, and may return through a callback, reconciliation, or a customer report. @absolutejs/handoff keeps those observations joined without pretending your application can inspect an external page directly.

sections.heading: Evidence and reconciliation
sections.text: external_api, callback, and reconciliation evidence is authoritative. external_surface_report evidence records what a customer or operator saw without silently overriding external-system truth.

sections.heading: Recording
sections.text: createHandoffRecorder() accepts optional storage and observer contracts. Recording returns per-sink delivery state instead of throwing when an observability sink fails, so visibility cannot break the business operation. The recorder also exposes low-cardinality counters by source and outcome. Messages and references redact payment-number-shaped text and bearer credentials. Applications must still keep raw callbacks, credentials, payment details, and customer data in their own protected stores.

sections.heading: Package boundaries
sections.text: @absolutejs/handoff owns the shared protocol. Domain packages keep their own meaning and adapters: Commerce decides what paid, declined, and settled mean. Dispatch decides what sent, bounced, and complained mean. Show 3 more CRM decides what synchronized or conflicted means. Voice and Meeting decide what joined, recorded, and transcribed mean. Those packages translate external-system evidence into this neutral vocabulary. Outcomes

sections.heading: HCSS
sections.text: @absolutejs/hcss v0.1.0 beta Commerce & Growth Typed HCSS HeavyJob read client with client credentials, bounded transport, and validated pagination.

sections.heading: Installation
sections.text: BASH bun add @absolutejs/hcss

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Read-only HeavyJob client for Bun / fetch-compatible runtimes. No Dirt Tracker business rules. Supports business units, jobs, v2 cursor-paginated cost codes, job materials, and material advanced budgets. Uses only heavyjob:read. Tokens are cached in memory, with concurrent acquisition coalesced. HTTP bodies, requests, pagination and item counts are bounded; redirects are rejected; errors never include credentials or provider bodies. No automatic retries. A failed or truncated read never returns a partial list. Create a client per credential set. Do not expose it to browsers. HCSS sandbox is a separate company credential context, not an assumed different API hostname. The caller must establish the correct company and authorization. Unknown units are preserved verbatim. Missing amounts and flags remain null, never zero/false. Budget IDs identify cost-code/material/purchase-order-detail relationships. Unknown response fields are discarded. This initial release has contract tests; live sandbox validation is pending access. No write endpoints are provided. Show 1 more Sources: credentials, business units, jobs, cost codes, materials, budgets. Outcomes
