sections.heading: Rapier3d
sections.text: @absolutejs/rapier3d v0.21.0 beta Frontend & UX Rapier 3D with matched free-body rotation, corrected contact witnesses and solver diagnostics

sections.heading: Installation
sections.text: BASH bun add @absolutejs/rapier3d

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: A focused distribution of Rapier 0.21.0 / engine 0.36.0 with solver-contact diagnostics, current-body geometry queries, accurate prescribed kinematics, and corrected contact-witness and force-free rotation calculations. The engine's original geometric manifolds and its clustered solver manifolds are distinct. The upstream JavaScript contact query only exposes the former, which can have no solver-contact entries even when the solver is resolving contact. This package exposes the latter separately. The callback receives a restricted solver view: normal, count, point, distance, friction, restitution, and tangent velocity. It does not promise original subshape identifiers or geometric surface normals. The flipped convention matches contactPair. Do not step, free, or mutate the world inside either callback. Nested read-only solver queries are supported; callback exceptions release query wrappers before propagating. Solver distances are the engine's cached contact update distances, not a continuous or post-step exact penetration guarantee. contactPair exposes geometric manifolds; solverContactPair exposes solver manifolds. Version 0.6 improves velocity-driven kinematics. Version 0.8 corrects previous-simplex witness preservation and reduces force-free rotation roundoff, as described below. Contact and CCD policy defaults remain unchanged. Runtime motion still needs independent geometric and energy checks. Show 2 more Version 0.8.1 refreshes articulated link velocities after final solver impulses and uses the integrated link geometry for center-of-mass velocity offsets. This fixes stale linvel()/angvel() state and inconsistent velocities on rotating fixed assemblies. It does not change the restitution iteration budget or provide a general energy-conservation guarantee for off-center articulated impacts. The ESM package includes WASM initialization and requires no separate asset URL. Concurrent init() calls share initialization. The package targets 3D f32 web/Node/Bun; it does not claim a 2D, f64, CommonJS or SIMD distribution.

sections.heading: Build and provenance
sections.text: Source base: dimforge/rapier commit b716d375efc0201003f0cd9ef7168eee0b62c177. Upstream Apache-2.0 licensing is retained. The distribution adds binding queries, package build/test tooling, and CCD profiler timer wiring. Version 0.6 also evaluates velocity-driven kinematic poses directly from each solver-pass origin. Version 0.8 additionally pins the corrected Parry collision source and applies the gyroscopic momentum increment without reconstructing the entire angular velocity through the inertia frame. Use Bun 1.4.4+absolute.1, Rust 1.94.0 with wasm32-unknown-unknown, and Python 3.12. Run bun install --frozen-lockfile, then bash absolutejs/scripts/build-native.sh. Cargo's exact lockfile is versioned, compilation defaults to one job (override with CARGO_BUILD_JOBS), and the wasm-bindgen 0.2.129 CLI archive is checksum verified before extraction. Caches and generated build output are reproducible; modified source and selected test receipts are committed. dist/provenance.json records the resulting WASM hash. API packaging verifies the post-bindgen native bytes against absolutejs/native-kernel.json before writing the distribution. A shared Cargo cache containing a research kernel therefore fails closed. Rebuild stable native source after research builds. Do not update the qualification hash merely to make a build pass: a changed kernel requires physical qualification and a recorded release decision. API-only releases retain the qualified native hash. See absolutejs/research/native-build-guard/ for positive and negative controls. Show 3 more The build copies this canonical documentation to the root README used by npm, so published package documentation stays synchronized. Run bun test absolutejs/tests after building. Tests compare queried and unqueried worlds under the same kernel, exercise actual clustered contacts, nested queries, exception cleanup, captured contact regressions and analytic rotation controls. The independent upstream-motion probe records intentional trajectory differences; exact old floating-point rounding is not a physical acceptance criterion. Browser-worker validation is separate from native GPU performance testing; no GPU is required by the engine. This is a maintained AbsoluteJS distribution, not an official Dimforge release.

sections.heading: Live anchors and explicit clustering control (0.2)
sections.headingTerms: live anchors and explicit clustering control (0.2)
sections.text: solverContactPoint1/2 return the native solver anchors transformed by current body poses. solverContactSeparation projects their difference onto the stored world solver normal. Negative means overlapping anchors; invalid indices return null. Anchor values include contact skin and hook offsets, so they are not necessarily points on the visible material surface. The normal is from the contact update; this is not a new narrow-phase query or a continuous material penetration bound. The old cached solverContactDist remains explicitly separate. world.integrationParameters.contactClustering exposes the existing engine switch. It defaults to true, exactly as upstream. Set it only between steps; disabling it may increase solver workload and is not a general penetration fix. Snapshot restore preserves the setting. The game is not instructed to turn it off by this release. The independent every-step cube/cavity audit demonstrates the distinction: about 0.459mm current penetration is visible in live anchors when the cached distance is zero. Disabling clustering retains about 0.469mm peak penetration in that case. Neither extra telemetry nor changing clustering is presented as a physics cure. Show 1 more minCcdDt exposes the engine's minimum CCD substep duration in seconds. Its upstream default stays 1/60/100, even when the outer timestep is changed. The setter rejects negative, non-finite and f32-overflowing values. Smaller values can introduce instability; changing it is an explicit experiment, not an automatic quality preset. Both controls are retained through native snapshot serialization.

sections.heading: Restored collider ownership (0.2.1)
sections.text: Snapshot restoration now preserves null for an unowned collider's parent(). Previously an absent native handle could be coerced to body zero during JavaScript wrapper reconstruction. Real body-zero and fixed-body attachments remain intact. This changes wrapper metadata only; native ownership, WASM and solver behavior are unchanged. Repeated snapshot restoration and browser workers are regression tested.

sections.heading: Actual CCD substeps (0.3)
sections.text: Enable world.profilerEnabled = true, step the world, then read world.ccdSubsteps(). It reports the native count of CCD passes in the last completed profiled step, rather than the configured maximum. Zero means CCD did not act, not that the world failed to advance. It returns null when unavailable: before a profiled step, while profiling is disabled, or after toggling profiling until a new step completes. Setting an already enabled profiler to true is idempotent. Restored worlds start with profiling disabled and no sample. Event-enabled stepping is covered too. This is opt-in telemetry; no physics policy or defaults change. The counter does not expose individual substep durations or times of impact. CCD timing now accumulates activation/impact-planning and motion-clamping work across all passes in a step. The TOI timer also accumulates instead of resetting for every clamp pass. Both are recorded only with profiling enabled. The timing fix leaves contact equations and trajectories unchanged; package tests compare profiled/unprofiled poses and official upstream trajectories.

sections.heading: Contact policy controls (0.4)
sections.text: The following existing native settings are now exposed through world.integrationParameters. Defaults and solver algorithms are unchanged. Property — Default — Meaning contactRecycling — true — Reuse contact manifolds while relative poses stay within the native reuse bounds. Show 4 more normalizedContactRecycleDistance — 0.05 — Relative-pose drift bound, multiplied by lengthUnit; zero prevents recycling. warmstartCoefficient — 1 — Fraction of cached impulses reused by the solver, from zero to one. Change settings between simulation steps. The boolean setter rejects coercible non-booleans; numeric setters reject non-finite/out-of-range input, including f32 overflow for the distance. Native snapshots preserve all three settings. These controls support explicit diagnosis and application-specific qualification. Disabling recycling increases contact-generation work and can change contact features; disabling warm starting changes convergence. Neither is a general fix for penetration. Evaluate the entire requested simulation horizon and geometric intersections, alongside live/cached contact diagnostics. A process that exits successfully after an early physical guard is not a completed physical test.

sections.heading: Current-body shape contact queries (0.5.0)
sections.text: This additive query composes each collider's local pose with its current parent body pose. It observes direct body edits before the next world step without propagating poses, stepping the simulation, or altering cached solver contacts. Parentless colliders use their own world pose. The optional third argument reuses a ShapeContact result. Prediction must be finite and nonnegative, in world units. Use this for bounded explicit diagnostics, not every render/physics tick. It allocates shape queries and returns a world-space native shape contact, not a solver manifold, continuous sweep or authored-material overlap bound. Collision filters, hooks and contact skin are not applied. Native unsupported shape pairs can return null as well as separated pairs; null is not a general disjointness proof. Existing contactCollider retains its stored-collider-pose semantics. The distinction matters for rotating contacts: projecting current anchors onto a stored normal can report no penetration while a fresh shape query finds overlap. Both observations are useful, but answer different questions. Release 0.5.0 keeps the 0.4.0 native kernel byte-for-byte unchanged; it does not include the private relative-motion, EPA or clamp-graph solver experiments.

sections.heading: Prescribed velocity-driven paths (0.6)
sections.text: Velocity-driven kinematic bodies now evaluate their prescribed center-of-mass translation and rotation from the start of each solver pass. This removes angular phase error from repeatedly linearizing the prescribed rotation and limits substep-dependent accumulation drift. Existing linear/angular speed caps still apply. Dynamic bodies, position-driven endpoints, multibody integration and soft-frame proxies retain their prior integration paths. No API changes are required. This changes motion involving velocity-driven kinematic bodies, including the contact response of bodies they touch. Floating point rounding remains; this is not a general contact or continuous-collision accuracy guarantee. Native qualification records, independent analytic path controls, negative tests against 0.5.0, and bounded CPU observations are retained in absolutejs/research/kinematic-precision/. The private tagged contact research is excluded from this release. Direct rotation evaluation adds CPU work for velocity-driven kinematic bodies. Profile kinematic-heavy scenes; increasing solver subdivisions is not a free accuracy improvement. The recorded CPU probes are not browser FPS guarantees. Show 1 more Native builds use pinned Rust and wasm-bindgen versions and remap checkout/cache paths to stable virtual prefixes before checking the qualified WASM checksum. Custom compiler flags are preserved, but their output must still match the qualified kernel. A checksum mismatch stops API packaging; it does not silently adopt a different native solver.

sections.heading: Lightweight build identity (0.7)
sections.text: Version 0.7 adds package metadata without changing the qualified 0.6 native kernel. Package version and kernel release are deliberately separate fields. This release does not include the experimental gyroscopic increment correction; game contact regressions keep that native change under investigation. The frozen metadata includes package version, qualified kernel release, native WASM SHA-256/byte count, upstream/binding versions and whether the kernel changes the pinned upstream solver. The same values are available as RAPIER.buildInfo and the root named buildInfo export. Package and kernel releases can differ when an API-only upgrade reuses a qualified kernel. The lightweight subpath contains metadata only and works before init(). It reports the packaged kernel; supplying custom bytes to init(input) does not change that identity and must be recorded separately.

sections.heading: Contact witnesses and force-free rotation (0.8)
sections.text: Version 0.8 introduced the absolutejs/parry collision correction at revision dbd99a8dfce020da3698056471262435d56d3f69, based on upstream 0.31.1. Tetrahedron-to-face reduction now preserves support points needed by GJK's previous-simplex calculation. Previously, an overwritten point could be combined with its old barycentric weight, inventing a deep contact. A captured floor/hull case reported -14.719921 cm despite separation; the corrected native replay reports a small positive separation. Snapshot decoding and query read-only behavior remain byte-exact. No contact tolerance, CCD default or game rejection threshold is changed by this correction. The rotation correction applies only the computed gyroscopic momentum increment. Principal-axis and isotropic force-free bodies therefore avoid artificial spin-up from repeatedly reconstructing the entire velocity through inertia and its inverse. Genuine asymmetric precession remains active and is checked against a converged double-precision Euler/RK4 reference. In the recorded 336-case, 0.1-second free-spin matrix, worst relative energy error falls from about 0.004033 to 0.000562. One tilted long-box control has about 1.305 ppm more energy error. These measurements cover specific shapes, rates and iteration budgets; they are not a universal energy-error bound, a performance claim, or a substitute for coupled-contact acceptance. f32 conditioning and time integration errors remain. Show 1 more buildInfo.collisionLibraryVersion and buildInfo.collisionSource identify the exact locked collision library alongside the native WASM hash. They are lightweight serialized strings and require no WASM initialization. Packaging rejects ambiguous multiple Parry source entries. Release qualification evidence and retained experiment results are recorded in absolutejs/research/simplex-gyro/.

sections.heading: Articulation damping controls
sections.text: world.multibodyJoints.generalizedDamping(jointHandle) returns an owned Float32Array for the entire articulation containing that joint, including its floating root. A removed joint returns undefined. These coefficients are raw native coefficients, separate from rigid-body damping: native free angular generalized coordinates default to 0.1 even when RigidBody.setAngularDamping(0) is used. They are not dimensionless decay rates: angular coefficients act against inertia in native world units. The same numeric coefficient need not produce the same decay after changing the world length scale. setGeneralizedDamping(jointHandle, values) returns true on success. It rejects wrong lengths, negative/nonfinite values, native float overflow and removed handles without mutation. Coordinate order is the native generalized order; read the vector again after adding, removing or changing joints. The setter does not wake sleeping bodies; wake the affected bodies explicitly. Neither method changes the native default policy for newly created coordinates. For an explicitly undamped diagnostic, read the vector, replace it with a zero vector of the same length, and verify the readback. This is a diagnostic control, not a recommendation to remove damping from every game mechanism.

sections.heading: Coupled articulation impacts (0.10)
sections.text: Coupled contacts can disturb each other: a single late restitution sweep can leave order-dependent velocities when two bodies strike one light articulation. Version 0.10 repeats the existing normal/restitution solve to a projected velocity residual, with a bounded iteration budget. In these adaptive phases, a local double-precision normal-impulse accumulator retains corrections that would otherwise round away. Native velocities, response matrices, warmstart storage, persistent snapshots, and the JavaScript API retain their existing formats. This is not a double-precision engine or an energy clamp. Adaptive compression applies only to one-group, single-worker, generic-only frictionless contacts, with no soft/FEM bodies or independent joint rows. The configured PGS count remains a minimum; the cap is the larger of that count and 256. Adaptive restitution applies only to one-group, single-worker, generic-only contacts and is capped at 256 sweeps. Both stop at a projected velocity residual of 1e-6 lengthUnit. Ordinary and mixed/parallel contact paths retain their previous iteration policy. Reaching the cap is not a guarantee of convergence for arbitrary mass ratios or scenes. The added regression cases cover opposing impacts, creation-order reversal, restitution 0/0.5/1, unequal masses, timestep and substep changes. Existing integration, contact preparation, damping defaults and geometry are unchanged; known general articulation integration limitations remain. Show 1 more Accuracy has a CPU cost. A bounded CPU-only paired benchmark of 1/8/32 disconnected heavy-light-heavy impacts measured candidate median step times of 0.62/2.48/7.87 ms, versus 0.41/0.84/1.72 ms for 0.9.0, whose velocity error in that fixture was about 6.94 m/s. The candidate error was below 0.000002 m/s. These are host-specific step measurements excluding rendering and snapshot restoration, not a frame-rate guarantee. Production scenes still need physics budgets and profiling. Detailed qualification and limitations are in absolutejs/research/contact-convergence/.

sections.heading: Adaptive contact observations (0.11)
sections.text: Enable world.profilerEnabled, complete a step, then call world.contactConvergence() for an owned ContactConvergenceStats object. The result is null before a completed profiled step, while profiling is disabled, after toggling profiling until another step completes, and after snapshot restoration. Reading or mutating this returned object cannot change the world. No profiling data is serialized into physical world snapshots. Fields are compressionSolves, compressionIterations, compressionLimitHits, maxCompressionResidual, and restitutionSolves, restitutionIterations, restitutionLimitHits, maxRestitutionResidual. Counts accumulate across eligible solve phases within the full step, including CCD passes and solver substeps. They count phases/groups, not physical islands or individual contacts. Zero solves means no eligible adaptive path was executed; it does not certify that all contacts converged. Ordinary and mixed/parallel paths are outside these adaptive observations. Residual fields are the maximum terminal projected normal-velocity error among measured phases, in native world length units per second. A limit hit means the phase exhausted its configured budget while still above the existing 1e-6 lengthUnit threshold. The API reports that fact; it does not change tolerances, budgets, impulses or physical policy. The configured compression minimum may exceed 256 and is still honored. Show 2 more The added diagnostics exactly preserve physical result records across 548 paired collision/free-motion cases versus 0.10.0. Profiler-on/off snapshot parity and CCD aggregation are also tested. In the 20/1/20 kg fixture, the counters reveal 164 compression passes and 256 restitution sweeps, with a terminal restitution residual near 2.15e-6 m/s. A tiny physical error can therefore coexist with an exhausted iteration budget. Treat that as useful evidence, not as zero or automatic failure of the simulation. Unprofiled paired median costs at 1/8/32 islands were 0.65/2.49/7.09 ms versus 0.66/2.45/7.28 ms for 0.10.0 in the qualification run. These host-specific small samples do not establish a speedup or frame-rate guarantee. Query allocation occurs only when the caller requests observations.

sections.heading: Bounded managed-step profiling
sections.text: createPhysicsStepProfiler(world, options) borrows an initialized world. Call profiler.step(eventQueue?, hooks?) wherever you would explicitly call world.step(), then profiler.snapshot() to obtain an owned report. It creates no render loop, listeners, transport, or ownership of the world/event queue. This is suitable for workers and offline jobs as well as application-managed stepping. Every managed call records wall time spent inside World.step. Selected calls also capture native phase timings, CCD substeps, convergence counters and world units/settings. Native timings are nested: do not add solver, assembly, resolution and CCD durations together. Native samples are observations of those selected calls, not estimates of unsampled solver work. The summary wall-time sum excludes profiler setup, native capture and report construction; it is not whole-job time or an FPS measurement. The default cadence and capacity are both 32. Sampling stops when capacity is reached; samplesOmittedForBudget counts later eligible calls. Use sampleStartStep to inspect a later window. Capacity is bounded to 256; zero keeps wall-time accounting without enabling native profiling. A failed selected call consumes a slot. There is no unbounded event queue or per-body duplication. Show 2 more Each selected call restores the previous native profiler setting, including when stepping throws. Unselected calls leave it alone. If profiling was already on, the caller retains fresh native observations; otherwise turning it back off invalidates native live queries, but the owned captured sample remains readable. Original step exceptions (including non-Error values) propagate unchanged. Clock and native-capture failures are counted instead of stopping a successful physical step; missing/invalid observations are null, never invented zero times. A custom now must return monotonic milliseconds and have no side effects. Reports remain usable after freeing the borrowed world. Always attach the actual build identity when storing or sending a report through your existing diagnostics system. Sampling has a cost: use explicit application policy and measure it. The sampler was introduced in 0.12.0 without changing the 0.11.0 native kernel. Sampling itself does not change solver thresholds, contact policies or physical state serialization. Later native revisions remain identified by buildInfo.

sections.heading: Compound inertia reconstruction (0.13)
sections.text: The collision dependency now pins absolutejs/parry revision c566aabd77be8ac7a427c2b704860c47e34657b9. Mass-property aggregation uses a scale-normalized, bounded Jacobi decomposition with double-precision workspace. It corrects principal frames for small tensors and repeated or nearly repeated moments. Public f32 types, mass, COM and nonnegative principal-moment policy are unchanged; compound mass properties and resulting motion can change when the previous decomposition was inaccurate. No JavaScript API is added. The focused native suite covers 2,688 tensor/aggregation cases in f32 and f64. The package tests also reconstruct two- and three-collider physical tensors across scale, orientation and insertion order. The small-object baseline could exceed 50% relative tensor error; this is a reproduced fixture, not an estimate of error across all objects. Angular integration and articulated COM-transport limitations are separate and remain under investigation. This calculation runs when mass properties are recomputed. It is not a render optimization: recompute after geometry/mass changes, not unnecessarily every frame. Qualification records, measured cost and limits are retained under absolutejs/research/inertia-reconstruction/.

sections.heading: Matched isolated-body rotation and observations (0.14)
sections.text: An isolated, awake dynamic body with gyroscopic forces enabled now uses a bounded implicit midpoint angular update with its matching Cayley attitude. This substantially reduces free-flight angular energy and world-momentum drift. The path requires physical stored inertia, unlocked angular axes, zero external torque and angular damping, and ordinary rotation limits. Contact-connected, jointed, articulated, soft/FEM and fast-rotation bodies retain their existing solver path. This does not correct coupled angular/contact integration or the remaining articulated COM-transport defect. A rejected update does not partially mutate state. Nonphysical stored moments, rotation limits and failed/invalid solves are observed explicitly; the existing correction/cap ordering applies for the rest of that island solve. The next solve re-evaluates eligibility. No energy or momentum clamp is introduced. With world.profilerEnabled = true, world.freeRotationStats() returns owned counts (acceptedSteps, nonphysicalInertiaRejections, rotationLimitRejections, invalidOrFailedSolves), maximum Newton updates, and maximum accepted residual in radians/second. It returns null before a completed profiled step, after restoration, while profiling is disabled or after toggling it. Counts include solver substeps and CCD passes; zero acceptance does not establish conservation. The bounded createPhysicsStepProfiler includes these observations as each sample's native.freeRotation, with the same sample and ownership limits. Show 3 more The 96-case native matrix reduces worst relative angular-energy drift from 3.2% to 0.00026%; 542 excluded/rejected control states match the previous release exactly. On a synthetic 32-body CPU/WASM workload the median paired additional cost is approximately 0.7 microseconds per body/substep (2.9x batch ratio). These are fixture measurements, not game-wide guarantees or hardware FPS. Admission, numerical/storage limits, actual-engine tests, failed assumptions and cost records are preserved in absolutejs/research/rigid-midpoint-engine. Floating-root center-of-mass coordinates (0.14.1) Articulation root linear velocity is measured at its center of mass. For an object whose authored origin differs from its mass center, time integration must rotate the local COM offset while advancing that physical center. The root origin update includes R_old localCom - R_new localCom; otherwise moving an object's modeling origin changes its physical trajectory. Fixed roots and zero-offset roots retain their existing arithmetic. This correction does not replace the articulation's angular integrator or eliminate remaining aggregate momentum/energy drift. Coordinate-covariance, movable-joint and snapshot replay regressions are recorded in absolutejs/research/rigid-assembly.

sections.heading: Isolated fixed-assembly integration and observations (0.15)
sections.text: The solver additionally admits isolated floating assemblies made only of fixed links, with gyroscopic forces enabled, no damping/armature/friction, no locks or fast rotation, and no external loads except uniform gravity shared by every link. Contacts, external joints, movable links, differing gravity scales and unsupported states retain their existing path. Aggregate inertia is assembled in authored local frames, then a matched angular update advances the assembly about its total center of mass. Linear gravity uses the existing semi-implicit kick-then-drift convention. This is not a contact or fracture model. world.freeAssemblyStats() reports owned attempt counts after a completed profiled step, with the same freshness rules as freeRotationStats(). The bounded profiler records a deep-owned native.freeAssembly object. Counters distinguish accepted steps, nonphysical-inertia rejections, rotation-limit rejections, and invalid/failed solves. Unsupported assemblies and invalid aggregate construction are excluded before an attempt; these exclusions do not increment rejection counts. Zero counts do not prove conservation. Counts include solver substeps and CCD passes. Qualification includes 198 package tests, 843 game tests, GPU-disabled browser checks, 80 byte-exact snapshot replays and matching independent distribution builds. The synthetic 16-assembly falling benchmark measured about 0.95 additional microseconds per assembly/substep (median paired batch ratio 1.12); this is not a hardware FPS result. Contact coupling, partial-subtree fracture and extreme thin-moment storage remain separate work. See absolutejs/research/aggregate-free-transport/README.md for evidence and limits.

sections.heading: Partial assembly splits and pending snapshots (0.16)
sections.headingTerms: partial assembly splits and pending snapshots (0.16)
sections.text: Removing a link from a moving fixed assembly can leave multiple assemblies. Newly released roots inherit their body's world COM and angular velocity; the surviving original root retains its coordinates, damping, armature, friction and surviving couplings. Newly free root coordinates use their normal defaults. Explicit fixed-to-dynamic activation also preserves prescribed body velocity. Initial articulation construction semantics are unchanged. An ordinary free fragment now retains the matched free-rotation path when an unrelated articulation shares its solver batch. Multibody links are excluded from ordinary-body initialization, and existing external-constraint, damping, torque, lock and speed exclusions still apply. This corrects a batch-dependent motion error without applying free-body integration to constrained bodies. takeSnapshot() now writes the ABSJS3DS envelope, version 1, including ordered pending connectivity edits and dirty impulse-joint state. Saving immediately after a cut therefore retains changes not yet consumed by a simulation step. Native Rust callers can capture/restore the opaque PendingIslandEvents companion with the corresponding serialized world sets. Capture neither flushes edits nor reconstructs the world's connectivity. Snapshot payloads still depend on the native engine layout: retain buildInfo with diagnostic captures; the envelope is not a promise of cross-engine save compatibility. Prior compatible raw captures remain readable for investigation, but edits omitted by their original writer cannot be recovered. All new saves use the versioned format. Show 1 more Qualification and retained failed assumptions are in absolutejs/research/assembly-split/. Tests measure the remaining material after body removal; they do not invent a fracture-energy budget or model cutting forces, plastic deformation or coupled-contact accuracy. Those remain separate physical models and qualification work.

sections.heading: Stable queued wake replay (0.16.1)
sections.text: Snapshots now serialize unordered pending wake/join membership in handle order. The default backend also consumes queued wake requests in handle order, retaining impulse-before-multibody priority. Previously, restoring a snapshot could reorder sleeping bodies when they woke, changing active-set records on subsequent steps. Only queued edits are sorted; there is no scan of every world body. The enhanced- determinism feature retains its existing insertion-ordered behavior. Ordered connectivity events and the version-1 snapshot payload layout are unchanged; this is not a general cross-engine snapshot-compatibility promise. Qualification includes 223 package tests, 843 game tests, exact sleeping-wake replays, native feature/worker checks, GPU-disabled browser replay and identical independent builds. Unaffected transport and impact states match published 0.16.0. Sorting has a measured cost: at 256 released bodies, median first-wake step time was 0.82 ms versus 0.98 ms, with about 26 microseconds added per pending snapshot capture. These are bounded CPU fixtures, not hardware FPS claims. See absolutejs/research/snapshot-order/ for original failures and full evidence.

sections.heading: Predictive convex contacts (0.16.2)
sections.text: Moving convex pairs now refresh separated predictive contacts instead of reusing stale closest features across the contact-recycling drift window. Captured tree fragments could previously penetrate while the cached anchors still reported separation. Exactly unchanged relative geometry and world rotations retain reuse, as do the existing empty-pair and touching-contact paths. This adds no public setting, solver-iteration increase or snapshot-layout change. The new rule applies only when both shapes are convex. Composite triangle, heightfield and compound contact recycling retains its prior behavior. A broader candidate regressed real generated-terrain support and was rejected; its captures and controls remain in the research record. Mixed touching/predictive sets and general composite-contact accuracy remain separate qualification work. Qualification includes 227 package tests, 844 game tests, exact captured replay, one/two-worker native checks, allocation-enabled no-std, GPU-disabled browser checks and 18 full tree-drop cases. Four generated/excavated terrain cases retain all measured physical fields and 491 poses exactly versus 0.16.1. The originally bad flat-floor tree cases improve from roughly 7–12 mm cached penetration to below 0.6 mm; other cases can change within their original limits. These cached measurements are not continuous authored-material penetration guarantees. Show 2 more Bounded paired CPU ratios versus 0.16.1 were about 0.99/0.99/1.05 for stationary predictions, resting stacks and falling boxes. The stack trajectory changes but passes its original stability limits. These fixtures do not measure hardware FPS or establish a general speedup. See absolutejs/research/predictive-recycle/ for source, failed candidates, controls and qualification receipts. Independent builds match all 49 distribution files and the packaged native payload byte-for-byte. Raw executable/data sections match; only unshipped wasm-bindgen custom metadata differs. Snapshot layout and public APIs are unchanged.

sections.heading: Approaching contact support (0.16.3)
sections.text: Contact-patch reduction now applies the same contact-skin, soft-body and velocity-prediction eligibility rule as final solver admission. Previously, reduction filtered outer points by current distance alone. An approaching tilted box could consequently receive support along just one edge even though points on the opposite edge qualified for the solver. The regression now retains four support points spanning both sides, across three scales and both insertion orders. Stationary and receding outer points remain excluded by the existing rule. This is a two-file solver correction. It changes no public API, snapshot layout, material coefficient, solver budget or admission tolerance. Published Parry c566aabd is unchanged; the separate GJK-normal, persistent triangle-frame and conservative-CCD experiments are excluded. This release does not solve the remaining generated-heightfield or rotational direct-sweep limitations. Qualification includes 236 package tests, 844 game tests, exact snapshot replay, GPU-disabled browser tests, native one/two-worker controls and allocation-enabled no-std. The 24 paired terrain controls add no rejection, but the existing raw variant-0/1920 rejection remains. Four actual generated/excavated work requests and 18 flat-floor tree cases pass their original limits. Twenty of 24 paired terrain rows retain their measured physical fields exactly; others change. These checks do not establish continuous authored-material separation. Show 2 more Bounded paired CPU ratios versus 0.16.2 were approximately 1.03, 1.05 and 0.95 for stationary predictions, resting stacks and falling boxes, with identical final physical fields. The affected tilted-patch ratio was 0.95. These shared-host observations are not hardware FPS or a universal speedup claim. See absolutejs/research/predictive-support/ for complete evidence and limitations. Independent builds match all 49 distribution files and the packaged native payload byte-for-byte. Raw executable/data sections match; only unshipped wasm-bindgen metadata differs.

sections.heading: Rotational intervals and cached contact directions (0.17.0)
sections.headingTerms: rotational intervals and cached contact directions (0.17.0)
sections.text: Orientation-changing 3D direct sweeps now use separating-plane motion bounds to detect the captured case where a rotating bar crosses a surface between two clear endpoint poses. Translation-only sweeps retain the existing path. The distance-query budget remains 25, with explicit failure if safe progress cannot be established. Composite traversal is a separate limitation; this is not a universal continuous-separation guarantee. Stalled convex queries preserve the direction associated with the support bound used for classification. This fixes a captured tree/triangle query that reported about 202 mm penetration while independent plane projection bounded required separation to about 0.013 mm. Both corrections are qualified together: the rotational change alone exposed this cached-direction error in the full oak excavation test. The combined engine passes it and all 844 game tests. Package API, snapshot layout, contact tolerances and solver budgets are unchanged. The raw variant-5/960 terrain clearance rejection remains identically present; physical outcomes elsewhere may change. Bounded CPU control scenes retain identical physical results and comparable timings. The targeted tilted-contact fixture costs about 51% more after extended warmup, about 0.037 ms extra per restored step in that fixture. This is a measured correctness tradeoff, not a browser FPS or general performance guarantee. Show 10 more Qualification includes 432 direct-sweep cases, captured old/new contact regressions, 237 package tests, GPU-disabled browser checks, native one/two-worker controls, no-std, 24 tree/rate comparisons, four generated/excavated requests, 18 flat-tree cases and an independent build matching all shipped files. Evidence: absolutejs/research/rotational-contact/. Numerical contact softness world.integrationParameters.contactSoftness and staticContactSoftness read or atomically replace { naturalFrequency, dampingRatio }. The first controls dynamic contacts (native default 30 Hz / 10); the second controls contacts with a fixed body (native default 60 Hz / 10). Change them between steps. Reads return owned copies; values must be representable finite native coefficients, with positive frequency and nonnegative damping. Both values are validated before either changes. Snapshots preserve both settings. Bounded step profiles record each distinct settings pair once in a bounded contactSettings table; samples carry native.contactSettingsIndex. Reports deeply own that table, including after the world is freed. This avoids repeating configuration in every sample and keeps telemetry within existing event budgets. These are numerical regularization parameters, not measured material elasticity. Higher frequency can reduce transient penetration but may produce jitter or prevent sleeping. Qualify motion, contact, sleeping and cost across actual scenarios before changing a product's policy. Defaults are unchanged. 0.18.0 contact correction and adoption limits The collision library rejects an exactly duplicated CSO point before it can form a degenerate tetrahedron and lose a valid terrain contact. Both friction builders select static/dynamic coefficients directly, avoiding dependence on an unused coefficient through floating-point cancellation. Native defaults remain unchanged. In the game's actual tree matrix, the collision correction fixes one missed-contact case but makes another case exceed the game's clearance limit at default softness (-21.007 mm). The game therefore qualifies an explicit 600 Hz / 10 static-contact policy alongside this engine: all 24 tree/rate cases and 18 cut-tree cases pass and sleep. This is a bounded product policy, not a universal stiffness recommendation. The default-policy failure is retained in the investigation records. Qualification: 242 package tests, 847 game tests, four generated/excavated terrain requests, GPU-disabled browser controls, native serial/two-worker checks, no-std, and independent builds matching all shipped files. Three ordinary CPU controls are within roughly 1% of 0.17.0 in this run. See absolutejs/research/contact-softness-controls/ for measured fixture costs, source hashes, intermediate failures and scope limitations. Queued 0.19.0: explicit quadratic resistance solveQuadraticDragImpulse analytically integrates one quadratic relative-flow resistance channel with positive supplied effective inverse mass. It returns the signed impulse, implicit relative speed, dissipated energy and separate body / reservoir work. It is pure and does not infer shape, exposure or coefficients. Use consistent units and the complete effective mass response; verify native application precision. See absolutejs/research/quadratic-drag-2026-10-31/README.md for the derivation, scope and evidence. Native engine qualification stays 0.18.0.

sections.heading: Prepared solver schedules (0.20.0)
sections.text: The opt-in world.solverSchedule() query returns owned observations from the last completed profiled step. Like ccdSubsteps(), it returns null before such a step, when profiling is disabled or toggled, and after snapshot restoration. createPhysicsStepProfiler retains distinct owned records in solverSchedules, referenced by each sample's native.solverScheduleIndex (omitted means entry 0). The table is always present and cannot exceed the retained sample count; repeated observations do not repeat the full record. groupVisits counts prepared nonempty rigid-body solve groups across CCD passes. rigidBodyVisits sums their rigid-body slots, while rigidBodySubsteps weights those slots by each group's prepared substep count. These are visits, not unique body identities. minSubsteps/maxSubsteps report the group range; minSubstepDt/maxSubstepDt are durations in seconds. All four range fields are null when no nonempty rigid group was prepared. Soft-particle-only work and internal PGS sweeps are outside these counts. This reads the actual group layout, including additional iterations propagated through constraint-connected bodies. It does not change that layout, force sampling, native timestep or contact policy. It is not a per-body mapping, elapsed CPU timing, proof of force/energy accuracy, or forecast of the next step. In particular, a previous group's substep count must not silently select gameplay fluid-force timing when contact connectivity or CCD can change. Show 5 more The native observer is qualified by independent native builds and exact full-state comparisons across 18 fixtures / 9,240 steps against 0.19.0. Sampled local CPU costs and limits are recorded in absolutejs/research/solver-schedule/. The previous private artifacts remain archived; release availability is separate from source qualification. Bounded diagnostic profile transport encodePhysicsStepProfile(profile) converts a readable report into an owned, versioned numeric packet. decodePhysicsStepProfile(value) validates an unknown packet and reconstructs owned readable observations. For example: The codec preserves every defined observation without rounding, including null measurements, failed samples, signed zero and explicit versus omitted default schedule references. It excludes arbitrary application metadata and user strings. The format tag is absolutejs-physics-step-profile/1; one fixed '-0' cell tag preserves signed zero through JSON. Arrays are bounded to 256 entries, tuple lengths and enums are fixed, and indices/scalars are validated. Malformed packets throw TypeError. This is transport validation, not a claim of native provenance or physical correctness. Apply normal metadata redaction outside the codec. Readable PhysicsStepProfile remains the simulation-facing API. In 0.20 its always-present solverSchedules table and optional sample index are part of that schema; older readable profiles without this table are not silently upgraded. Keep the format tag with stored packets and decode before displaying their fields.

sections.heading: Convex boundary export (0.21)
sections.text: collider.convexMeshData() returns an owned {vertices: Float32Array, indices: Uint32Array} pair from one native hull reconstruction. Use it when both buffers are needed; separate vertices() and indices() calls each reconstruct the hull. The query observes the current shape, so replacing a collider's shape requires no cache invalidation. Mutating returned arrays does not change the collider. Nonconvex shapes return undefined. Rounded convex shapes return the inner polyhedron, excluding the round radius. The mesh is a reconstructed boundary of the stored Float32 points, not a copy of internal contact faces. Reconstruction uses double precision and exact-sign dimension checks for thin point clouds; returned positions remain original Float32 coordinates. It does not upgrade the physics engine's storage or solver to double precision. Boundary measurements and native mass measurements remain distinct; applications must continue to validate both. buildInfo.convexExportPrecision identifies this reconstruction as float64. The f32 and f64 collision-library dependencies use the same recorded source pin. Captured export, browser-worker, simulation-parity and CPU timing evidence lives in absolutejs/research/convex-export/. Release availability is separate from source qualification; publication may be deferred. The unchanged physical engine retains its existing settling limits. Outcomes

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: A focused distribution of Rapier 0.21.0 / engine 0.36.0 with solver-contact diagnostics, current-body geometry queries, accurate prescribed kinematics, and corrected contact-witness and force-free rotation calculations. The engine's original geometric manifolds and its clustered solver manifolds are distinct. The upstream JavaScript contact query only exposes the former, which can have no solver-contact entries even when the solver is resolving contact. This package exposes the latter separately.

sections.heading: Build and provenance
sections.text: Source base: dimforge/rapier commit b716d375efc0201003f0cd9ef7168eee0b62c177. Upstream Apache-2.0 licensing is retained. The distribution adds binding queries, package build/test tooling, and CCD profiler timer wiring. Version 0.6 also evaluates velocity-driven kinematic poses directly from each solver-pass origin. Version 0.8 additionally pins the corrected Parry collision source and applies the gyroscopic momentum increment without reconstructing the entire angular velocity through the inertia frame.

sections.heading: Live anchors and explicit clustering control (0.2)
sections.headingTerms: live anchors and explicit clustering control (0.2)
sections.text: solverContactPoint1/2 return the native solver anchors transformed by current body poses. solverContactSeparation projects their difference onto the stored world solver normal. Negative means overlapping anchors; invalid indices return null. Anchor values include contact skin and hook offsets, so they are not necessarily points on the visible material surface. The normal is from the contact update; this is not a new narrow-phase query or a continuous material penetration bound. The old cached solverContactDist remains explicitly separate. Hardening checklist

sections.heading: Production guidance
sections.text: Make every external boundary explicit Pin the deployed @absolutejs/rapier3d version, replace example or memory-backed dependencies with durable implementations, bound external calls, protect credentials, and emit enough evidence to retry or recover safely. Follow in order

sections.heading: Troubleshooting path
sections.text: 1 Overview A focused distribution of Rapier 0.21.0 / engine 0.36.0 with solver-contact diagnostics, current-body geometry queries, accurate prescribed kinematics, and corrected contact-witness and force-free rotation calculations. The engine's original geometric manifolds and its clustered solver manifolds are distinct. The upstream JavaScript contact query only exposes the former, which can have no solver-contact entries even when the solver is resolving contact. This package exposes the latter separately. 2 Prescribed velocity-driven paths (0.6) Velocity-driven kinematic bodies now evaluate their prescribed center-of-mass translation and rotation from the start of each solver pass. This removes angular phase error from repeatedly linearizing the prescribed rotation and limits substep-dependent accumulation drift. Existing linear/angular speed caps still apply. Dynamic bodies, position-driven endpoints, multibody integration and soft-frame proxies retain their prior integration paths. 3 Rotational intervals and cached contact directions (0.17.0) Orientation-changing 3D direct sweeps now use separating-plane motion bounds to detect the captured case where a rotating bar crosses a surface between two clear endpoint poses. Translation-only sweeps retain the existing path. The distance-query budget remains 25, with explicit failure if safe progress cannot be established. Composite traversal is a separate limitation; this is not a universal continuous-separation guarantee.

label: Rate Limit Overview

sections.heading: Rate Limit
sections.text: A first-class, from-scratch, 2026 rate limit for Bun + Elysia. GCRA by default — the algorithm Stripe uses — with token bucket and sliding-window also bundled. IETF draft-09 RateLimit-* headers, IPv6 grouping by /64 , X-Forwarded-For trust modes, BigInt nanosecond TAT, and a lazy-TTL LRU memory store with no background sweeper.

sections.heading: Choose the traffic behavior you mean
sections.headingTerms: choose the traffic behavior you mean
sections.text: The algorithms share a store contract but intentionally expose different traffic semantics. Best for: A precise general-purpose limit with smooth behavior and constant storage. Tradeoffs: The model is less intuitive to explain than a visible request counter. Requirements One theoretical-arrival-time value per key

sections.heading: How proxy-aware client identity is derived
sections.headingTerms: how proxy-aware client identity is derived
sections.text: Only explicitly trusted network hops may influence the client identity used as a quota key. Observe Receive the socket peer address and any forwarded-address headers. Bound trust Walk back only the configured number of trusted proxy hops. Reject spoofing Discard attacker-controlled addresses to the left of that boundary. Derive key Normalize IPv4 or group IPv6 by prefix before consulting the store.

sections.heading: Quick Start
sections.text: rateLimit() is an Elysia plugin — wire it with .use() and every request is gated before it reaches your handlers. The default key is the requester's IP; the default algorithm is GCRA. TS import { Elysia } from ' elysia ' ; import { rateLimit , gcra } from ' @absolutejs/rate-limit ' ; new Elysia () . use ( rateLimit ( { // GCRA — the algorithm Stripe uses. Exact, O(1) memory per key, // no boundary effects. Burst of 5, sustained 10 req/s. algorithm : gcra ( { requestsPerPeriod : 10 , periodMs : 1000 , burst : 5 } ) , // 'ip' uses extractIp() with the trustedProxies + ipv6Prefix below. key : ' ip ' , trustedProxies : 1 , // honor one CDN/LB hop of X-Forwarded-For } )) . get ( ' / ' , () => ' ok ' ) . listen ( 3000 ) ; Over the cap, the plugin returns 429 with Retry-After + the IETF RateLimit-* headers. The remaining count stays current on the 200 responses too — so clients can throttle themselves before they get refused.

sections.heading: Algorithms
sections.text: Pick GCRA unless you have a reason not to. It's exact, O(1) memory per key (one BigInt — the TAT), no boundary effects, no float drift. Token bucket and sliding-window are bundled for when you specifically want their semantics (burst-then-throttle or N-in-the-last-M-seconds, respectively). Stack any of them with combined . TS // GCRA — default. Exact, BigInt nanosecond TAT, no float drift. import { gcra } from ' @absolutejs/rate-limit ' ; gcra ( { requestsPerPeriod : 100 , periodMs : 60_000 , burst : 20 } ) ; // Token bucket — classic. Allows refill-boundary bursts up to capacity. import { tokenBucket } from ' @absolutejs/rate-limit ' ; tokenBucket ( { capacity : 100 , refillPerSecond : 1.667 } ) ; // Sliding-window counter — approximation; intuitive on a status page. import { slidingWindow } from ' @absolutejs/rate-limit ' ; slidingWindow ( { requestsPerPeriod : 100 , periodMs : 60_000 } ) ; // Combined — passes only when every component passes. Stack limits: // 100 / minute per IP AND 10,000 / day per user-id import { combined } from ' @absolutejs/rate-limit ' ; combined ( { algorithms : [ gcra ( { requestsPerPeriod : 100 , periodMs : 60_000 , burst : 20 } ) , gcra ( { requestsPerPeriod : 10_000 , periodMs : 86_400_000 } ) , ] , } ) ; GCRA — exact, BigInt nanosecond TAT, one number of state per key, no boundary effects. The default. Token bucket — classic. Allows brief bursts at refill boundaries. Pick this when you want "fill the bucket, fire it all at once" semantics. Sliding window — counter approximation. Easy to explain on a status page ("you have N requests left in the last M seconds"). Combined — composes any number of algorithms; passes only when every component passes. Stack a per-IP minute cap with a per-user-id daily cap in one plugin.

sections.heading: Cost, Keys & Hooks
sections.text: Heavy endpoints charge more than cheap ones with a cost function. The bucket goes into overdraft on a cost-N hit (you wait it off — same as Stripe's metered approach). Key derivation is a string preset ( 'ip' or 'authorization' ) or a function. skip bypasses the limit entirely; onAllow and onLimit are symmetric hooks for metrics + custom responses. TS new Elysia () . use ( rateLimit ( { algorithm : gcra ( { requestsPerPeriod : 100 , periodMs : 60_000 , burst : 20 } ) , // Per-route cost — heavy endpoints charge more. cost : ( ctx ) => { if ( ctx . request . url . includes ( ' /upload ' )) return 5 ; if ( ctx . request . url . includes ( ' /admin ' )) return 0 ; // free for admin return 1 ; } , // Custom key derivation — per-tenant, falling back to IP. key : ( ctx ) => ctx . request . headers . get ( ' x-tenant ' ) ?? extractIp ( { connectionIp : ctx . server ?. requestIP ?. ( ctx . request ) ?. address ?? null , headers : ctx . request . headers , trustedProxies : 1 , } ) , // Skip for admin tokens (sync — async work belongs in key). skip : ( ctx ) => ctx . request . headers . get ( ' authorization ' ) === ADMIN , // Fire a billing event on every allowed request. onAllow : ( _ctx , info ) => meter . record ( { type : ' handler ' , tenant : info . key , durationMs : 0 , cpuMs : 0 , ok : true , } ) , // Customize the 429 response. onLimit : ( _ctx , info ) => new Response ( JSON . stringify ( { ok : false , retryAfterSec : info . decision . retryAfterSec , } ) , { status : 429 , headers : { ' Content-Type ' : ' application/json ' } } ) , } )) ;

sections.heading: IETF Headers
sections.text: The default header set is IETF draft-09 — a combined RateLimit header carrying limit , remaining , and reset together, plus RateLimit-Policy describing the policy. Set headers: 'legacy' for the older X-RateLimit-* form (GitHub circa 2014), 'both' for a transition period, or false to suppress everything except Retry-After. BASH # IETF draft-09 (default — headers: 'standard') RateLimit: limit=20, remaining=18, reset= 15 RateLimit-Policy: 100 ; w = 60 ; burst = 20 Retry-After: 7 # only on 429 # Legacy GitHub-style (headers: 'legacy') X-RateLimit-Limit: 20 X-RateLimit-Remaining: 18 X-RateLimit-Reset: 15 Retry-After: 7 # Or 'both' to emit both — useful during a transition. # 'false' suppresses everything except Retry-After.

sections.heading: IP & Proxy Trust
sections.text: Most rate-limit libraries either trust X-Forwarded-For blindly (spoofable) or ignore it entirely (broken behind any CDN). trustedProxies: N honors only the last N hops — anything to the left is attacker-supplied and ignored. 0 disables XFF; 1 is the right default behind a single CDN/LB. IPv6 addresses are grouped by their /64 prefix by default — one user's RIR allocation gets one quota, not one quota per device. Configurable via ipv6Prefix . CDN headers ( cf-connecting-ip , fly-client-ip , true-client-ip , x-real-ip ) are honored when XFF is missing and a proxy is trusted. TS // trustedProxies — IPv6 /64 — CDN-aware import { extractIp } from ' @absolutejs/rate-limit/core ' ; // 0: ignore X-Forwarded-For entirely. Use the raw connection IP only. extractIp ( { trustedProxies : 0 , ... } ) ; // 1: trust ONE proxy hop. Take XFF[length - 1] (the originator). This is // the right default behind ONE CDN. Anything to the left is attacker-set. extractIp ( { trustedProxies : 1 , ... } ) ; // 2: trust TWO hops (CDN + load balancer). Same idea, take XFF[length-2]. extractIp ( { trustedProxies : 2 , ... } ) ; // IPv6 grouping: by default IPv6 is reduced to its /64 prefix — one user // allocation per RIR convention. 2001:db8::1 and 2001:db8::dead:beef both // hash to '2001:db8:0:0:0:0:0:0/64'. Configurable via ipv6Prefix. extractIp ( { ipv6Prefix : 128 , ... } ) ; // disable grouping // Honors cf-connecting-ip, fly-client-ip, true-client-ip, x-real-ip when // XFF is missing and a proxy is trusted.

sections.heading: Non-HTTP Usage
sections.text: The algorithms + store are exported separately at @absolutejs/rate-limit/core with no Elysia dependency. Use them directly for WebSocket-message rate-limiting, queue-consumer throttling, AI-call quotas — anywhere you need exact rate enforcement without HTTP. Each algorithm exposes peek() for status-page read-only inspection and reset() for admin clears. TS // Use the algorithms directly outside HTTP — WebSocket message rate-limit, // queue consumer throttle, AI call quotas. Import from /core to skip the // Elysia dependency entirely. import { gcra , memoryStore } from ' @absolutejs/rate-limit/core ' ; const aiLimiter = gcra ( { requestsPerPeriod : 60 , periodMs : 60_000 , burst : 10 } ) ; const store = memoryStore () ; async function callOpenAi ( userId : string , prompt : string ) { const decision = aiLimiter . check ( store , userId , Date . now ()) ; if ( ! decision . allowed ) { throw new Error ( ` Slow down — retry in ${ decision . retryAfterSec } s ` ) ; } return openai . chat . completions . create ( { ... } ) ; } // peek() = read-only inspection (no token consumed). const remaining = aiLimiter . peek ( store , userId , Date . now ()) . remaining ; // reset() = admin clear. aiLimiter . reset ( store , userId ) ; Next Outcome Playbooks · Govern an AI Agent

sections.heading: Reliability
sections.text: @absolutejs/reliability v0.1.0 beta Platform & Infra Provider-neutral atomic inbox, transaction, and idempotent-operation primitives for AbsoluteJS.

sections.heading: Installation
sections.text: BASH bun add @absolutejs/reliability

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Provider-neutral reliability primitives for side-effecting integrations: checked-out PostgreSQL transactions that keep every statement on one connection; scoped, payload-fingerprinted idempotent operations with fencing and an explicit Show 3 more indeterminate state after an external side effect may have started; an atomic webhook inbox with leases, replay claims, completion, and retention purge. The package has no database-driver dependency. Pass a pool with connect() to createPostgresTransactionRunner(), apply the exported schemas, and construct the stores. A plain pool-level query() is intentionally not accepted because it cannot guarantee transaction connection affinity.

sections.heading: Idempotent operations
sections.text: Use createPostgresIdempotentOperationStore() in multi-process production deployments. The store fences concurrent claims and preserves an indeterminate result when an external side effect may have started but its final outcome is unknown.

sections.heading: Durable webhook inbox
sections.text: createMemoryWebhookInboxStore() covers tests. createPostgresWebhookInboxStore() and drainWebhookInbox() provide atomic leases, retries, replay protection, completion, and retention purging for production webhook consumers.

sections.heading: Transaction affinity
sections.text: createPostgresTransactionRunner() checks out one connection for the complete transaction. This prevents transaction statements from accidentally crossing pooled connections. Outcomes

sections.heading: Rendering
sections.text: @absolutejs/rendering v0.3.0 beta Frontend & UX Render-destination coverage policies and callback-preserving material ownership for Three.js applications.

sections.heading: Installation
sections.text: BASH bun add @absolutejs/rendering

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Small Three.js material-lifecycle utilities for AbsoluteJS applications and 3D authoring tools. These complement R3F and drei; they do not provide a scene graph, camera controls, effects composer or renderer replacement.

sections.heading: Coverage follows the destination
sections.text: A multisampled canvas does not make a reflection texture multisampled. An alpha-to-coverage shader used unchanged in a single-sample target can draw partially covered foliage as solid pixels. The policy runs after the previous material callback and before Three selects the program. It updates the material only when the effective coverage mode changes. Three can cache the corresponding program variants. It does not inject shaders, allocate textures, traverse the scene, monkey-patch a renderer, or call synchronous GPU queries per draw. Shader customizations must retain their non-ALPHA_TO_COVERAGE fallback. The policy uses declared render-target sample counts, bounded by renderer support; callers must create targets with supported attachment formats. Canvas antialias attributes are cached per renderer, but a lost context is not cached as a permanent capability result. Disabled preferences remain disabled on all destinations. Shadow passes that call renderBufferDirect require their own depth-material policy; this callback targets normal material draws. Show 1 more Rebinding updates the existing preference without stacking callbacks. The returned disposer is idempotent and restores the original flag and callback only while it still owns the callback slot; it will not overwrite a later owner.

sections.heading: Clone customized materials safely
sections.text: This retains onBeforeCompile, customProgramCacheKey and onBeforeRender. A registered destination policy is cloned independently, including when the source was last drawn into a non-MSAA target. Changing the clone's preference cannot affect the source. This does not clone arbitrary object callbacks, custom depth materials or scene state.

sections.heading: Compatibility and scope
sections.text: Qualified against Three r186. No React dependency and no animation loop. Runtime cost is a small callback and destination check per affected draw; switching sampling modes can select another cached shader program. Hardware frame-rate improvements are not claimed. Game-specific foliage algorithms, lighting, world generation and simulation remain outside this package. Use bun run check:package to build declarations and run the ownership/policy tests. Browser evidence is retained under docs/.

sections.heading: Scoped captures and readback
sections.text: renderTargetScope(renderer, run) restores the render target, cube face, mip, viewport, scissor and scissor-test state even if synchronous work throws. The callback must finish renderer mutations synchronously; do not hold a scope over an await. readTargetPixelsScoped(renderer, target, width, height, buffer, textureIndex?) submits a byte/float read from a neutral target and restores the caller through Three's target setter. This avoids restoring a resolve framebuffer in place of its multisample draw attachment, or treating a cube framebuffer array as a single framebuffer. readFloatTargetScoped(...) submits asynchronous float readback in the same neutral state, restores the caller immediately, and returns the exact supplied Float32Array on completion. It never restores stale renderer state after await. Allocate supported targets and correctly sized buffers before calling these helpers. The helpers do not choose formats, sample counts or capture resolution.

sections.heading: React Spring with demand-rendered Fiber scenes
sections.headingTerms: react spring with demand-rendered fiber scenes
sections.text: The optional @absolutejs/rendering/spring entry provides animated.mesh, animated.group, useSpring, easings, and createFiberSpringHost for other explicit Fiber primitives: It keeps React Spring's normal scheduler. Three prop updates invalidate the owning Fiber root through applyProps; DOM-only animation does not render a scene and can finish without a mounted Canvas. No useFrame, manual animation clock, global scheduler replacement, or unconditional render loop is installed. Do not also runtime-import @react-spring/three: that entry installs a global Fiber-driven scheduler even when its consuming component is never mounted. This adapter does not override or repair another module's global scheduler changes. Type-only imports from that package are safe. Test your actual application's eager import graph as well as isolated components. Show 1 more Use createFiberSpringHost(['instancedMesh', 'meshStandardMaterial']) to opt into additional hosts without registering every Three constructor. React, Fiber and React Spring peers are optional for the core material utilities, but required when using this subpath. @react-spring/three supplies host types only; it is not runtime-imported by this entry. The tested versions are React 19.3, Fiber 9.8.2, Three 0.186.1 and React Spring 10.1.2. Outcomes

sections.heading: Renown
sections.text: @absolutejs/renown v0.3.8 beta Dev Tools Earn XP and achievements for real, meritorious dev work in any editor, with per-project leaderboards. A gamified, quantified-self layer for programming: XP is earned by the craft and importance of your work — never by commit count — with thousands of achievements, deep activity recaps and competitive per-project leaderboards. It is editor- and agent-agnostic: a filesystem watcher tracks activity in any editor with zero plugins, and coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Copilot are first-class participants. The CLI talks to the hosted leaderboard at renown.absolutejs.com out of the box, and a GitHub Action can score every contributor on each push.

sections.heading: Installation
sections.text: BASH bun add -g @absolutejs/renown

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: [](https://github.com/absolutejs/renown/actions/workflows/ci.yml) Earn XP and renown for real, meritorious dev work — in any editor. A gamified, quantified-self layer for programming: XP is earned by the craft and importance of your work (never by commit-count), with thousands of achievements, deep activity recaps, and competitive per-project leaderboards. By AbsoluteJS. Grew out of a personal coding-agent experiment; now its own thing — editor- and agent-agnostic, with Claude, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Aider, Gemini, and friends all treated as first-class participants. Show 1 more ▶ Live leaderboard: renown.absolutejs.com

sections.heading: Quick start
sections.text: The CLI talks to the hosted leaderboard out of the box — no config needed. Then wire it into your editor so XP accrues as you work: …or drop the Action into any repo to score every contributor on each push:

sections.heading: Why it's not cheese-able
sections.text: XP comes from a craft engine that scores each commit by substance (generated files / lockfiles / minified / reformat ≈ 0), with bonuses for tests/docs/new code and penalties for tiny/junk/duplicate commits and daily grinding — then a project- importance multiplier: open-source ×, GitHub stars (log scale), and contributing to someone else's repo ×. Only commits you authored count.

sections.heading: Architecture (Bun monorepo)
sections.text: core — engine: craft scoring, achievements, stats, leveling, shared types. daemon — editor-agnostic activity tracker: a filesystem watcher over your git repos emits activity heartbeats with zero editor plugins (works in VS Code, Neovim, JetBrains, anything) and detects commits. Editor plugins can POST richer heartbeats to it (WakaTime-style) later. Show 6 more cli — renown / renown recap TUI + renown heartbeat. core/agents.ts — universal coding-agent registry used by local stats, agent skills, achievements, and install docs. server — Bun API + Drizzle/Neon: /submit, /top, /top?project, /achievements (catalog + global rarity %). db — Drizzle schema + Neon client.

sections.heading: Database (Drizzle + Postgres on Neon)
sections.text: players, achievements (catalog incl. the 10k; unlock_count → rarity %), player_achievements (unlocked_at → date achieved), projects, player_projects (per-project boards). Rich local activity/recap data stays on-device; only scores and unlocks sync.

sections.heading: ⚠️ Secrets
sections.text: DATABASE_URL lives in .env (gitignored) — never commit it. Rotate the Neon password before this repo is public.

sections.heading: GitHub Action — auto-sync from CI
sections.text: Drop the renown Action into a repo and every push refreshes that repo's contributors' renown — their score, Co-Authored-By attribution, freshly-pulled serialized pets, and the repo's own /project leaderboard — with no manual renown sync and no secrets in the workflow. The Action reads GitHub's own context (the pusher + the authors GitHub names in the event) and asks your renown server to recompute each linked contributor from the GitHub API using the server's token: their global renown and their per-repo commits/XP (scored by the same craft engine your local CLI uses — core/craftScore.ts is shared, so CI and local scoring can't drift; the board upsert is monotonic, so CI only ever adds contributors or raises stats). Contributors who aren't on renown simply no-op, and the step never fails your build. Self-hosting? Add with: { endpoint: https://your-host/api }. Prefer no extra action? Call the CLI directly — same effect: Locally, renown ci-sync --endpoint does the same against a GITHUB_-populated env.

sections.heading: Craft-based XP
sections.text: A craft engine scores each commit by substance — generated files, lockfiles, minified code and reformats score near zero — with bonuses for tests, docs and new code, and penalties for junk or grinding.

sections.heading: Not cheese-able
sections.text: Only commits you authored count, and a project-importance multiplier weighs open source, GitHub stars (log scale) and contributions to repos that are not your own.

sections.heading: Works in any editor

sections.heading: Verified leaderboards
sections.text: renown link verifies your GitHub account, and public boards rank server-recomputed, GitHub-verified XP — no board ranks purely self-reported data.

sections.heading: 10k achievements
sections.text: A catalog of 10,000 achievements with global rarity percentages, skills, quests and collectible pets, browsable from the renown TUI.

sections.heading: Renown VS Code Extension
sections.text: renown-vscode v0.1.0 beta Dev Tools Earn renown for real dev work — a live status bar + activity-driven sync, right in your editor. Talks to your renown server.

sections.heading: Installation
sections.text: BASH git clone https://github.com/absolutejs/renown-vscode-extension.git

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Earn renown for real dev work — a live HUD, activity-driven sync, and your 1/1 pets, right in your editor. Renown turns your verified GitHub contributions into a score, levels, and procedurally-generated 1/1 pets — each one minted from a real commit, so no two are alike. This extension brings that to where you already work. ---

sections.heading: What it does
sections.text: 🔥 Status bar HUD — your live renown (score + this-week delta), with total level and pet count in the tooltip. Signed in with GitHub, so the identity is proven, not typed. 🫀 Activity-driven sync — while you actively edit a repo, after a few minutes of work it asks the renown server to recompute your renown for that repo from your real GitHub commits (the same path as the renown ci-sync Action). A subtle spinner shows when it's syncing; a per-repo cooldown keeps it from re-running while you keep typing. 🐾 Sidebar panel — your badge, this week's recap, your pet roster, this repo's leaderboard, and the achievements you unlocked this week. Show 4 more 🎉 New-pet celebration — when a sync mints a new 1/1, the actual creature pops up (gently animated). Earning a pet is a moment, not a counter ticking up. Editing only triggers a refresh — it never sets your score. Everything is recomputed server-side from your GitHub-verified activity. The extension is a pure client; it can't inflate anything. See the trust model.    ---

sections.heading: Getting started
sections.text: Install (from source, until the Marketplace listing is live): Then open the folder in VS Code and press F5 to launch the Extension Development Host. Sign in — run Renown: Sign in with GitHub (or click Renown: sign in in the status bar). This uses VS Code's built-in GitHub auth — no separate account, no token to paste. Show 4 more Verify so you rank — accept the Verify so I rank prompt after signing in (or run Renown: Verify with Renown Server). This presents your GitHub session token to the server, which confirms it against GitHub, marks your account verified, and starts ranking you on the boards. The token is only read server-side to confirm your login — it's never stored. Point it at a renown server — set renown.endpoint to your server's API base. During local development that's http://localhost:7777/api against a bun run start in renown/web. (Once renown is hosted, this defaults to the hosted URL and won't need setting.) That's it — the HUD lights up, and editing a repo starts earning renown. ---

sections.heading: Commands
sections.text: Command — What it does Renown: Sign in with GitHub — Authenticate via VS Code's GitHub provider (proven identity). Renown: Verify with Renown Server — Link your GitHub to the server so your account ranks (confirms your token; never stores it). Show 6 more Renown: Sync This Repo Now — Recompute your renown for the active repo immediately. Renown: Preview New Pet — Open the celebration with your signature pet — no commit needed (handy for a look). Renown: Open My Profile — Open your public renown profile in the browser. Renown: Refresh Panel — Re-fetch the sidebar panel. Renown: Set GitHub Login (manual) — Override the identity (self-hosted / view-as). Renown: Open Settings — Jump to the renown settings.

sections.heading: Settings
sections.text: Setting — Default — Description renown.endpoint — "" — Your renown server's API base URL. renown.login — "" — Optional identity override. Normally blank — the signed-in GitHub identity is used. Show 3 more renown.heartbeatMinutes — 5 — Minutes of active editing in a repo before its renown is refreshed. renown.statusRefreshSeconds — 90 — How often the status bar re-fetches your renown. ---

sections.heading: How the sync works
sections.text: The extension sends no scores — only "please recompute @me / this repo." The server is the sole source of truth, and it only ever reads GitHub-verified data. ---

sections.text: A reachable renown server (renown.endpoint). There's no hosted endpoint yet — run one locally with renown/web (bun run start → http://localhost:7777/api). VS Code 1.85+ and the built-in GitHub authentication provider. Outcomes
